base.name: where-it-works
base.description: Installed in an app: it works in that app, as always, whichever `astryx` the person runs, because the app's version of Astryx answers there.
prose: Where your integration works
Installed in an app: it works in that app, as always, whichever `astryx` the person runs, because the app's version of Astryx answers there.

Installed next to the global install (`npm install -g @astryxdesign/cli your-package`), or in the same folder as the CLI by a tool that installs them together: it works in every folder outside a project. People and agents there see its components, templates, docs, themes, codemods, and discover source.

Installed only globally, inside an app that does not install it: it adds nothing there. When it supports the app's version and loads, `astryx discover` lists it as one the app could add, with the app's install command.
Installed both ways: the app's copy is the one used in that app. In your own package folder, your working copy is used.
Astryx loads a global integration with the same loader and checks as an app's, so nothing extra goes in your manifest.
base._title: Authoring › Make your integration work globally › Where your integration works

base.name: checklist
base.description: Declare the `@astryxdesign/core` (and, if you use it, `@astryxdesign/cli`) `peerDependencies` range your package really supports. Outside a project, Astryx skips your package when that range leaves out the global version, and `astryx…
prose: Checklist

Declare the `@astryxdesign/core` (and, if you use it, `@astryxdesign/cli`) `peerDependencies` range your package really supports. Outside a project, Astryx skips your package when that range leaves out the global version, and `astryx doctor` says why: too narrow, and global users lose it after an upgrade; too wide, and it loads against a Core it may not build with.
Keep imports in your docs and templates to packages an app installs with yours, since outside a project there is no app to check them against.

If you set `cliCommand`, know that outside a project it starts every command Astryx prints, and that two global integrations naming different commands cancel out, falling back to `astryx` (`astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/configuration/cli-command`). Inside an app, only the app's integrations count.
Try it globally before you publish, with the steps below.
base._title: Authoring › Make your integration work globally › Checklist

base.name: try-it
base.description: Pack your package, install it next to a global CLI, and look at it from an empty folder:
prose: Try it globally
Pack your package, install it next to a global CLI, and look at it from an empty folder:

npm pack  # only with npm: the tarball the registry receives
npm install -g @astryxdesign/cli ./your-package-1.0.0.tgz
mkdir -p /tmp/try-global && cd /tmp/try-global
astryx discover
astryx docs
astryx doctor
`astryx discover` lists your package as installed, with what it adds.
`astryx docs` lists your topics, and `astryx search <one of your component names>` finds them.
`astryx doctor`'s `computer-integrations` check lists your package as used, with no warning.
In an app that does not install it, `astryx discover` lists it as one the app could add, with the app's install command, and none of its components or docs show up.
Remove it again with `npm uninstall -g your-package`.

base.description: These appear while you start the package or run the CLI in it. Each row quotes what the CLI prints.
prose: Fix setup errors
These appear while you start the package or run the CLI in it. Each row quotes what the CLI prints.

No package.json found. Run this command inside an integration package. Run npm init -y (only with npm: writes package.json) and npm pkg set name=@acme/astryx-widgets (only with npm: edits package.json) first, in the package folder.
Error: Could not find @astryxdesign/core package Component commands read Core. Run npm install -D @astryxdesign/core in the package.
core_not_found: Could not resolve @astryxdesign/core, so component names could not be checked. Same fix. The check exits 1.

Error: unknown subcommand 'integration verify', or Error: Pass --check to verify the integration tarball. Your CLI is older than integration verify. Run npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli@latest. On the older CLI, the same check is integration pack --check.
Note: integration pack --check is deprecated. The old name still runs the same check. Switch to astryx integration verify; the old name will be removed in a later release.

base.name: fix-verify-failures
base.description: `astryx integration verify` prints each failure as a `[fail]` line. Add `--json` to see its issue code, such as `component_export_missing`.
prose: Fix integration verify failures
`astryx integration verify` prints each failure as a `[fail]` line. Add `--json` to see its issue code, such as `component_export_missing`.

component_export_missing: Component "AcmeCarousel" advertises import "@acme/astryx-widgets/components/AcmeCarousel", but that packed module does not export "AcmeCarousel". package.json has no exports map, or the module does not export the name. Keep export function AcmeCarousel, and add the entry: npm pkg set 'exports[./components/AcmeCarousel]=./components/AcmeCarousel.tsx' (only with npm: edits package.json). When the quoted name is a file name, such as acme-carousel, set the doc's name to the component the file exports. A type-only export does not count.

template_export_missing: Template "acme-dashboard" public import "@acme/astryx-widgets/templates/acme-dashboard" does not have a default export. Run npm pkg set 'exports[./templates/acme-dashboard]=./templates/acme-dashboard.tsx' (only with npm: edits package.json), and keep export default in the source. Start new packages with "exports": {} so each add writes these.

component_import_unresolvable or template_import_unresolvable: …Package subpath './components/AcmeCarousel' is not defined by "exports"… The exports map has no entry for it. Run npm pkg set 'exports[./components/AcmeCarousel]=./components/AcmeCarousel.tsx' (only with npm: edits package.json), or 'exports[./templates/acme-dashboard]=./templates/acme-dashboard.tsx' for a template.

component_import_unresolvable: …but a consumer cannot resolve it: Cannot find package '@acme/old-name' You renamed the package after the add wrote each doc's import. Change import in every component doc to the new name.
Declared templates root "templates" has 0 of 2 expected files in the pack list. Add "templates" to "files" in package.json. Run npm pkg set 'files[]=templates' (only with npm: edits package.json).

docs_tree_needs_cli: The package ships a namespace doc or a placed guide but declares no @astryxdesign/cli peer. Run npm pkg set 'peerDependencies.@astryxdesign/cli=>=0.6.4' (only with npm: edits package.json) and npm pkg set 'peerDependenciesMeta.@astryxdesign/cli.optional=true' --json (only with npm: edits package.json).

replaces_needs_cli: The package has a template that sets replaces but declares no @astryxdesign/cli peer. Run npm pkg set 'peerDependencies.@astryxdesign/cli=>=0.6.4' (only with npm: edits package.json) and npm pkg set 'peerDependenciesMeta.@astryxdesign/cli.optional=true' --json (only with npm: edits package.json). A stable CLI before 0.6.4 rejects replaces, drops that template, and hides your doc topics.

component_replaces_needs_cli (a warning): The package has a component that sets replaces but declares no @astryxdesign/cli peer, or a peer range that admits an earlier CLI. Run npm pkg set 'peerDependencies.@astryxdesign/cli=>=0.6.7' (only with npm: edits package.json) and npm pkg set 'peerDependenciesMeta.@astryxdesign/cli.optional=true' --json (only with npm: edits package.json) to turn the replacement on. Until then apps see no change (astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/components/replace-a-core-component).

keywords_needs_cli: The package has a template that sets keywords but declares no @astryxdesign/cli peer. Run npm pkg set 'peerDependencies.@astryxdesign/cli=>=0.6.6' (only with npm: edits package.json) and npm pkg set 'peerDependenciesMeta.@astryxdesign/cli.optional=true' --json (only with npm: edits package.json). What an older CLI does with the field is in astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/templates/document-the-template/template-doc-overview.

themes_need_cli: The package ships a theme but declares no @astryxdesign/cli peer. Run npm pkg set 'peerDependencies.@astryxdesign/cli=>=0.6.4' (only with npm: edits package.json) and npm pkg set 'peerDependenciesMeta.@astryxdesign/cli.optional=true' --json (only with npm: edits package.json). A CLI older than published 0.6.4 cannot read typed theme descriptors, so it drops your themes and can hide your doc topics.

section_ids_need_cli: The package has a doc section that sets id but declares no @astryxdesign/cli peer. The same fix as themes_need_cli, or drop the section ids: a CLI older than published 0.6.4 rejects them and hides your doc topics.

doc_tokens_need_cli: The package writes doc tokens (astryx …, {@pm …}, {@pm-only …}) in its docs, but its @astryxdesign/cli peer admits a CLI before 0.7.4. Run npm pkg set 'peerDependencies.@astryxdesign/cli=>=0.7.4' (only with npm: edits package.json) and npm pkg set 'peerDependenciesMeta.@astryxdesign/cli.optional=true' --json (only with npm: edits package.json). A CLI before 0.7.4 prints each token as written, so readers see raw tokens.

base.name: fix-problems-in-an-app
base.description: These appear in an app that installs your package, or in the doctor checks that predict them.
prose: Fix problems in an app
These appear in an app that installs your package, or in the doctor checks that predict them.

Error: No component named "AcmeCarousel" for a component your package documents. Its doc still names its file. Set name to the export, such as name: 'AcmeCarousel' in acme-carousel.doc.mjs. A family member is listed only when the module its family doc imports exports it (astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/components/describe-the-component/component-family).

astryx component Dialog opens Core's Dialog, not yours. A name that Core, a legacy docs package, or another package's file already has stays theirs. Run astryx component Dialog --package @acme/astryx-widgets, or give your component a name of its own.

Error: Template "dashboard" is ambiguous — narrow it with --type and/or --package. Your template id matches a Core id. Rename it, such as acme-dashboard, or set replaces: 'dashboard' to take its place. astryx doctor integration templates warns about this before you publish.

invalid_doc_graph: placement.parent "namespace:nope" names no namespace; @acme/astryx-widgets declares "acme". The guide stays hidden until its placement names a namespace and slot your package declares. For "…" names no doc, fix the link target.

Error: Unknown topic "acme". The docs of @acme/astryx-widgets did not load; run astryx doctor integration docs in that package to see why. One invalid doc hides all of your docs. Run astryx doctor integration docs in the package and fix the invalid_doc it names.

cli-command warns: Loaded integrations declare different CLI commands Two packages the app loads set different cliCommand values, so the CLI prints the package manager's command. Agree on one command, or remove the package that does not belong. See astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/configuration/cli-command.
invalid_cli_command Your cliCommand is not one line of plain text of at most 120 characters, so it is ignored. Fix the value; the rest of the manifest still loads.

astryx upgrade runs none of your codemods The app must list your package in integrations in astryx.config, or pass --integration @acme/astryx-widgets. It runs a codemod folder only when its version is after --from and at most the installed @astryxdesign/core.

Your docs section, templates, or themes are missing only in some apps Those apps run a CLI too old to read them (astryx docs authoring/ship/checks lists which field needs which CLI). Update @astryxdesign/cli there, and keep your optional @astryxdesign/cli peer so npm checks the app's CLI against it when the app installs your package.
What each check catches is in `astryx docs authoring/ship/checks`.

base.name: quick-start
base.description: An integration starts as a normal npm package. Make a folder for it, create a package.json inside that folder, give the package a name, make it an ES module, then install the Astryx CLI, Core, and TypeScript for development.
prose: Quick start
Make the package

An integration starts as a normal npm package. Make a folder for it, create a package.json inside that folder, give the package a name, make it an ES module, then install the Astryx CLI, Core, and TypeScript for development.

mkdir acme-widgets && cd acme-widgets
npm init -y  # only with npm: writes package.json
npm pkg set name=@acme/astryx-widgets type=module  # only with npm: edits package.json
npm pkg set 'exports={}' --json  # only with npm: edits package.json
npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli @astryxdesign/core typescript@6

Set `"type": "module"`: the `.js` files the CLI generates, such as a built theme, are ES modules, and Node fails to load them in a package marked `"type": "commonjs"`, which `npm init -y` (only with npm: writes package.json) writes on npm 11.
Start with `"exports": {}`: each component and template you add then writes the public import that `integration verify` resolves.
Run the CLI as `astryx`, which runs the `@astryxdesign/cli` you installed as a devDependency.
Component commands read Core, so they need `@astryxdesign/core` installed.

The checks compare your docs with your code through TypeScript's JavaScript compiler API, which `typescript` 5.0 through 6 has. TypeScript 7 does not ship that API: on TypeScript 7, also install `@typescript/typescript6`, its TypeScript 6 API package, and the checks use it.
Add your first integration item
An integration can ship several kinds of items. Start with a component named `AcmeCarousel`.
astryx integration add component AcmeCarousel

component contribution added

[ok] AcmeCarousel

Declare component root ./components in astryx.integration.mjs.

- components/AcmeCarousel.doc.mjs
- components/AcmeCarousel.tsx
- package.json
- astryx.integration.mjs

`integration add` creates the component source, its `.doc.mjs`, the package export, and `astryx.integration.mjs`. Update the generated doc so the CLI understands the component, then write the component itself.
Read it back the way an app will.
astryx component AcmeCarousel
You now have an integration package with one exported component.
Check it in every build (required)

Run `integration check --strict` in every build (`astryx docs authoring/ship/checks`): a doc, prop, template, or link that drifts from the code then fails your build, not your users' apps. Set it up now, as the `typecheck` script, and run it.

npm pkg set scripts.typecheck="astryx integration check --strict"  # only with npm: edits package.json
npm run typecheck
[ok] 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 skipped. Every check passed.
Run `typecheck` in CI and before every publish. When you add a `tsconfig.json`, put `tsc --noEmit && ` in front of the check so the same script checks your types.
What each check covers, and what `--strict` adds: `astryx docs authoring/ship/checks`.
Verify and pack the package

Run `integration verify` to check that an app would see the component, then make the `.tgz` file you install next. `--pack-destination ..` writes it beside the package folder, so the next pack does not ship it.

astryx integration verify
npm pack --pack-destination ..  # only with npm: builds the publish tarball

Integration package ready

[ok] @acme/astryx-widgets@1.0.0

4 packed files; 3/3 required files present.

`integration verify` installs the packed package in a temporary app and confirms the component resolves through its public import there (`astryx docs authoring/ship/checks`). It publishes nothing and leaves no `.tgz` file, so `npm pack` (only with npm: builds the publish tarball) writes `../acme-astryx-widgets-1.0.0.tgz` for the next step.
Use it in an app
Install Core, the CLI, and your `.tgz` file in a new app. The app loads your package because it is a dependency, with no config.

cd ..
mkdir my-app && cd my-app
npm init -y  # only with npm: writes package.json
npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/cli ../acme-astryx-widgets-1.0.0.tgz
astryx component AcmeCarousel
**Import:** `import {AcmeCarousel} from '@acme/astryx-widgets/components/AcmeCarousel';`
The next sections explain each package field and the integration file. To build the real component, continue with `astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/components`.
base._title: Authoring › Quick Start › Quick start

base.name: fill-in-package-json
base.description: An integration is an ordinary npm package. These six fields control how it is named, developed, checked, and published.
prose: Fill in package.json
An integration is an ordinary npm package. These six fields control how it is named, developed, checked, and published.
`peerDependencies` are packages the app supplies. `devDependencies` are packages you use while building the integration.
name Your package name, such as @acme/astryx-widgets Each add writes it into the import of the doc it generates. Rename before you add, or update each import after.
version The release you publish, such as 1.0.0 Apps see it; astryx.integration.mjs never repeats it.
exports Start with {} Each component and template add writes its public import here, and integration verify resolves it.
files Optional: the paths to publish Keeps private files out. When the list exists, each add appends its root and astryx.integration.mjs.

peerDependencies @astryxdesign/core when your code imports it; @astryxdesign/cli, optional, when you ship a feature that needs a newer CLI (astryx docs authoring/ship/versioning) The app supplies these packages for your integration.
devDependencies @astryxdesign/cli, @astryxdesign/core, and typescript Lets you run the CLI, build components, and run the checks while working on the integration.

Peer ranges and releases are covered in `astryx docs authoring/ship/versioning`; `files` and publishing in `astryx docs authoring/ship/publishing`. Add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && astryx integration check --strict"` to `scripts` so each run checks your types and that your docs, props, and links still match the code. It needs `typescript` and a `tsconfig.json`; see `astryx docs authoring/ship/checks`.
base._title: Authoring › Quick Start › Fill in package.json

base.name: the-integration-file
base.description: The first `integration add` creates `astryx.integration.mjs`, and each later add updates it. You do not need to write or edit this file during the quick start.
prose: The integration file
The first `integration add` creates `astryx.integration.mjs`, and each later add updates it. You do not need to write or edit this file during the quick start.
Files in the package
`package.json` defines the npm package, including its name, version, dependencies, published files, and exports.
`astryx.integration.mjs` tells the CLI where the package keeps each kind of integration item.
The integration item files live under those roots. For example, a component can have `AcmeWidget.tsx` for its source and `AcmeWidget.doc.mjs` for its documentation.
Fields in the integration file

The file tells the CLI where this package keeps its integration items. Edit it only when you want a custom root or another optional setting. Paths are relative to package.json, and later adds keep a custom path you already set.
Every field is in `astryx docs authoring integration`.
Use the CLI
You can edit the package files by hand, but the CLI handles the normal workflow. These links always open the canonical command docs.

base.name: pick-a-check
base.description: Run these in the package folder. The four `doctor integration` checks read your source, and `integration check` runs all four; `integration verify` checks the package npm would publish.
prose: Pick a check
Run these in the package folder. The four `doctor integration` checks read your source, and `integration check` runs all four; `integration verify` checks the package npm would publish.

astryx doctor integration validate The manifest loads, each root holds contributions the CLI can read, and each doc matches its authoring type. Notes list a malformed cliCommand (invalid_cli_command) and, for each topic, a command written with a package runner (runner_command), bare (plain_command) or for one package manager (package_manager_command), and a token that does not parse (doc_token; see astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/doc-syntax). Notes fail nothing by default; integration check --strict --next fails on the ones marked next, and the next minor release counts them A declared root is missing (missing_root), a contribution does not load (invalid_doc, invalid_component, invalid_theme), or two templates in the package replace one Core id (ambiguous_template_replacement) The manifest has a key this CLI does not know (unknown_manifest_key), or a doc field does not match the doc's authoring type: a field the type does not have, a missing required field, or a value outside the field's type. It also warns on what no reader can serve: a prop listed twice (duplicate_prop), a propDescriptions key that names no documented prop (unknown_translated_prop), a section with no content (empty_section), two sections of a topic with one key (duplicate_section_key), or a .doc.zh.mjs or .doc.dense.mjs overlay beside no topic file (orphan_doc_overlay). Since 0.7.3 it also lists, from source and without failing, what the package tells apps to import that they cannot: a component's import (the doc's import, or the one the CLI derives) or a template's public import whose subpath package.json exports does not declare (component_import_not_exported, template_import_not_exported) or that names another package (component_import_other_package); an example that imports an undeclared subpath (example_import_not_exported); a template that imports a path outside the templates root (template_import_outside_root) or a path its package or Core does not export (template_private_import). It lists the same way a component's import whose module does not export the component (component_import_missing_name), an example or a template that imports a name its package does not export (example_import_missing_name, template_import_missing_name), and a template source with no default export (template_no_default_export). Each is a note, printed with its fix, that fails --strict from the next minor; an import it cannot judge, such as an exports target not built yet or a deep path into a dist/ not built yet, is listed under publicImports as not checked. It checks docs with your installed typescript, or, where that is missing or has no JavaScript compiler API (TypeScript 7), with an installed @typescript/typescript6; without either, it prints [skip] Docs not type-checked. With no astryx.integration.mjs it prints a hint and exits 0

astryx doctor integration components No component name clashes with a Core component, each replaces names one Core component, and each component doc's props match the component's TypeScript props Core is not installed (core_not_found). In a package that declares the CLI range that turns replacement on, a replaces target is missing (missing_component_replacement_target) or invalid (invalid_component_replacement), or two components replace one Core component (ambiguous_component_replacement) A name clashes with Core, a component sets replaces in a package without that range (inactive_component_replacement, plus any missing, invalid, or duplicate replaces reported as a warning), or a documented prop differs from the code: it is missing there (not_in_code), the doc omits a prop the package declares (not_in_doc), or its required (required_mismatch), type (type_mismatch), or literal default (default_mismatch) disagrees, or a {@link} in a component doc names no doc (invalid_doc_graph). It reads props with your installed typescript; without it, it prints [skip] Props not compared

astryx doctor integration templates Each replaces names a Core template of the same type A replaces target is missing (missing_template_replacement_target) or of the other type (invalid_template_replacement), or two templates replace one id (ambiguous_template_replacement) A template id matches a Core id without replaces

astryx doctor integration docs Your docs tree, every link, topic names against Core, passages two topics repeat word for word, padding phrases and low-density topics, and written pointers to docs A topic takes a Core topic name without replaces or extends, a doc is invalid (invalid_doc), or a namespace or placement fails, which hides the doc (invalid_doc_graph) A link names no doc (invalid_doc_graph), two topics repeat a passage word for word (copied_passage), prose pads with a listed phrase or falls under the density floor (doc_fluff), or prose, a description or summary, or the text of a component doc writes astryx docs <name> where a link would be checked (stray_doc_pointer)

astryx integration check Everything the four doctor integration checks prove, in one command, for your build Any of the four would exit 1 on its own. With --strict, also any warning, and any check that did not run, such as a package with no astryx.integration.* Anything the four warn about, unless you pass --strict

astryx integration verify The packed package holds every file, shows the same contributions, resolves every public import, and declares the CLI it needs Anything validate fails on, no manifest, a file left out of the .tgz file, an import that does not resolve, or a missing CLI peer Anything validate warns about, or a component sets replaces and the package does not declare the CLI range that turns it on (component_replaces_needs_cli)

Pass a package name, such as `astryx doctor integration validate @acme/astryx-widgets`, to check an installed copy from an app instead. To fix a props finding, see `astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/components/describe-the-component/check-the-props`.

base.name: run-every-check-in-ci
keywords: Run every check in every build (required)
base.description: Every integration runs `integration check --strict` in its own build, so every build keeps your docs, types, and links in sync; this is required, not optional. The strict check fails on every copied passage the docs check lists (`astryx…
prose: Run every check in every build (required)

Every integration runs `integration check --strict` in its own build, so every build keeps your docs, types, and links in sync; this is required, not optional. The strict check fails on every copied passage the docs check lists (`astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/docs/check-your-docs`). Run `integration verify` before you publish. Install devDependencies first, because the components check needs Core, and `tsc --noEmit` needs `typescript` and a `tsconfig.json`. In package.json:
"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && astryx integration check --strict"
`integration check` runs `validate`, `components`, `templates`, and `docs` in that order, prints each result, then a summary, and exits 1 when any of them would.
`--strict` also exits 1 on any warning and on any check that did not run. Without it, warnings keep exit code 0: use that while you fix the warnings a package already has.

Its exit codes and JSON are a contract for your build: a new check, or a new failure code, joins only in a minor release that names it in the release notes. A patch can still ship a Core component, template, or CLI topic whose name conflicts with one of yours.

`integration verify` runs `validate` but none of the other three: a Core name clash, a `replaces` that names no Core template, a topic that takes a Core name, or a hidden guide still passes it. Run both before you publish: `astryx integration check --strict && astryx integration verify`.
Bare `astryx doctor` in the package also warns about a doc section over 32 KB, which no check above measures.
titles: Run every check in every build (required)
base._title: Authoring › Ship › Check an integration › Run every check in every build (required)

base.name: what-integration-verify-does
base.description: `integration verify` packs your package with npm, unpacks it into a temporary app, and checks that the app sees everything your source has. It publishes nothing and leaves no `.tgz` file or temporary folder behind.
prose: Verify the packed package

`integration verify` packs your package with npm, unpacks it into a temporary app, and checks that the app sees everything your source has. It publishes nothing and leaves no `.tgz` file or temporary folder behind.
It runs `npm pack` (only with npm: the tarball the registry receives) the way `npm publish` (only with npm: npm is the client the registry publishes from) would, including your `prepack` script.
It checks that every contribution file is in the `.tgz` file. A root missing from `files` fails with `Add "templates" to "files" in package.json.`
It lists the components, templates, themes, docs, and codemods the temporary app sees, and compares them with your source.

It resolves each component's `import`, and each template's public import, the way Node does, and checks that the module exports the component under the name its doc documents, or a default export for a template. A type-only export does not count.

For each theme, it rebuilds the source, compares the built module and production CSS with the authored outputs, and proves the module, CSS, and optional font CSS exports resolve from the packed package.

It fails a package that needs an `@astryxdesign/cli` peer and lacks it: `>=0.6.6` for a template that sets `keywords`, and `>=0.6.4` for a template that sets `replaces`, a docs section, a placed guide, a doc section with an `id`, or a theme.

`integration pack --check`, the name this check had before published 0.6.5, still runs it and prints a note; it will be removed in a later release. The options and exit codes are in `astryx docs cli/commands/integration-verify`.
base._title: Authoring › Ship › Check an integration › Verify the packed package

prose: Check before you publish

Publish only a package that passes every check, then preview the upload with `npm publish --dry-run` (only with npm: publishing goes through npm, which every Node install carries). The dry run lists the files and the tag without uploading.

astryx doctor integration validate && astryx doctor integration components && astryx doctor integration templates && astryx doctor integration docs && astryx integration verify
npm publish --dry-run --access public  # only with npm: publishing goes through npm, which every Node install carries

npm notice Publishing to https://registry.npmjs.org/ with tag latest and public access (dry-run)
+ @acme/astryx-widgets@1.0.0
Set a new `version` for each release; `astryx docs authoring/ship/versioning` covers what counts as breaking. What each check proves is in `astryx docs authoring/ship/checks`.

base.name: keep-private-files-out
base.description: With no `files` list, npm packs every file your ignore files do not exclude, including an old `.tgz` file or an `.env` file. List what ships instead.
prose: Keep private files out
With no `files` list, npm packs every file your ignore files do not exclude, including an old `.tgz` file or an `.env` file. List what ships instead.

npm pkg set 'files[]=components' 'files[]=templates' 'files[]=themes' 'files[]=docs' 'files[]=codemods' 'files[]=astryx.integration.mjs'  # only with npm: edits package.json
npm pack --dry-run  # only with npm: builds the tarball npm publishes
List only the roots you ship, and always `astryx.integration.mjs`. npm adds package.json, and a README and LICENSE when you have them.
Each later `integration add` appends its root to the list.
`integration verify` fails when a root is missing from the list, and names the root to add to `files` (the message is in `astryx docs authoring/help/troubleshooting`).

base.name: publish-to-npm
base.description: A scoped package is private by default, so publish it with `--access public`. Without `--tag`, npm tags the release `latest`, which is what `npm install @acme/astryx-widgets` installs.
prose: Publish to npm
A scoped package is private by default, so publish it with `--access public`. Without `--tag`, npm tags the release `latest`, which is what `npm install @acme/astryx-widgets` installs.

# Publish a release
npm publish --access public  # only with npm: publishing goes through npm, which every Node install carries

# Or set the access once in package.json
npm pkg set publishConfig.access=public  # only with npm: Yarn has no pkg command
To let apps try a release first, publish it under `next`, then point `latest` at it once ready.

# Only apps that ask for next get it: npm install @acme/astryx-widgets@next
npm publish --tag next  # only with npm: publishing goes through npm, which every Node install carries

# Make that version the default
npm dist-tag add @acme/astryx-widgets@1.1.0 latest  # only with npm: dist-tags are set with npm, which every Node install carries
npm dist-tag ls @acme/astryx-widgets  # only with npm: dist-tags are set with npm, which every Node install carries
base._title: Authoring › Ship › Publish an integration › Publish to npm

base.description: Install the version you published in a clean app, and run the same commands you ran against the `.tgz` file.
prose: Check the published package
Install the version you published in a clean app, and run the same commands you ran against the `.tgz` file.

mkdir check-release && cd check-release
npm init -y  # only with npm: npm, which every Node install carries, writes the package.json
npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/cli @acme/astryx-widgets@1.0.0
astryx component AcmeCarousel
astryx doctor integration validate @acme/astryx-widgets
The full list of commands to run in an app is in `astryx docs authoring/ship/test-in-an-app`. To help apps move to the new version, see `astryx docs authoring/ship/upgrading`.

keywords: Install the packed package in an app
base.description: Pack the package beside its folder, so the next pack does not ship it, then install it in an app together with Core and the CLI. The app loads your package because it is a dependency.
prose: Install the packed package in an app
Pack the package beside its folder, so the next pack does not ship it, then install it in an app together with Core and the CLI. The app loads your package because it is a dependency.

# In the package
npm pack --pack-destination ..  # only with npm: the tarball the registry receives

# In an app folder beside it
npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/cli ../acme-astryx-widgets-1.0.0.tgz
Install the CLI in the app too: `astryx` runs the CLI from the app's `node_modules`.
The app holds a copy, not a link. After each change, pack again and run the same `npm install`.
Reading your work inside the package shows your source. The app shows what npm would publish.

base.description: From the app folder, run the commands your users run. Each should show your contribution under your package name.
prose: Check what the app sees
From the app folder, run the commands your users run. Each should show your contribution under your package name.

astryx component AcmeCarousel
astryx template --list --package @acme/astryx-widgets
astryx theme list --package @acme/astryx-widgets
astryx docs acme
astryx search deploying --type doc
component AcmeCarousel import {AcmeCarousel} from '@acme/astryx-widgets/components/AcmeCarousel';
template --list --package An acme-dashboard entry whose package is @acme/astryx-widgets
theme list --package An ocean entry whose package is @acme/astryx-widgets
docs acme Your section, with guides such as deploying
search deploying --type doc acme/deploying as the first result

`--package` narrows `template --list` and `theme list` to one package. `component --list` ignores it and lists Core too, so look a component up by name. Last, import `AcmeCarousel` in the app's code and build the app, as your users will.

prose: Run doctor in the app
`astryx doctor` checks the whole app, including every package it loaded. `doctor integration validate` checks your package as the app installed it.

astryx doctor
astryx doctor integration validate @acme/astryx-widgets

id:      implicit-integrations
status:  [info]
label:   Implicitly linked integrations
message: 1 integration loaded from installed dependencies with no astryx.config entry: @acme/astryx-widgets@1.0.0 from dependencies, contributing components, templates, themes, docs, codemods.
The `implicit-integrations` row names each package the app loads with no config. `[info]` is expected.
The `docs-progressive-disclosure` row warns when one of your doc sections is over 32 KB. The `doctor integration` checks do not measure size.
`doctor integration validate @acme/astryx-widgets` prints `[ok] No integration issues found.` when the installed copy is sound.

base.name: update-for-a-new-astryx-release
keywords: Update for a new Astryx release
base.description: When Astryx ships a release, bump your devDependencies, rerun the checks, widen your peer ranges, and ship a codemod for each change that breaks apps.
prose: Update for a new Astryx release
When Astryx ships a release, bump your devDependencies, rerun the checks, widen your peer ranges, and ship a codemod for each change that breaks apps.

# 1. Build and test against the new release
npm install -D @astryxdesign/cli@latest @astryxdesign/core@latest
# 2. Rerun the checks
astryx doctor integration validate
astryx doctor integration docs
astryx integration verify
# 3. Admit the new Core once the checks pass
npm pkg set 'peerDependencies.@astryxdesign/core=^0.6.0 || ^0.7.0'  # only with npm: edits package.json
# 4. Migrate apps across a change that breaks them
astryx integration add codemod rename-delay --to 0.7.0
Run every check in `astryx docs authoring/ship/checks`, not only the ones shown.
Codemod folders are named for Core versions: `astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/codemods`.
Release the result as a new version of your package; see `astryx docs authoring/ship/publishing`.
titles: Update for a new Astryx release
base._title: Authoring › Ship › Upgrading › Update for a new Astryx release

base.name: upgrade-an-app
base.description: After an app installs a new Core, `astryx upgrade` runs the codemods for the versions it crossed. It is a dry run by default; `--apply` writes the changes.
prose: Upgrade an app
After an app installs a new Core, `astryx upgrade` runs the codemods for the versions it crossed. It is a dry run by default; `--apply` writes the changes.

# Preview what would change; nothing is written
astryx upgrade --from 0.6.3 --integration @acme/astryx-widgets
# Write the changes
astryx upgrade --from 0.6.3 --integration @acme/astryx-widgets --apply

Integrations: @acme/astryx-widgets
<n> codemods to run
Applying integration codemods...
  Rename AcmeCarousel delay to interval (v0.7.0, @acme/astryx-widgets)
[ok]     [ok] src/Hero.tsx
`--from` is the `@astryxdesign/core` version the app had before, and the target is the installed Core.
`--integration` names your package. Without it, or an `integrations` entry in `astryx.config`, the upgrade skips your codemods, even when the app has your package installed.
`<n>` includes Core's codemods for the same versions, which run first.
Put this command in your release notes.
base._title: Authoring › Ship › Upgrading › Upgrade an app

base.name: know-which-files-upgrades-skip
base.description: Upgrades never write files that the app marks as generated, vendored, or ignored. When such a file still needs a codemod change, the upgrade stops with `ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED` and exit code 1.
prose: Know which files upgrades skip
Upgrades never write files that the app marks as generated, vendored, or ignored. When such a file still needs a codemod change, the upgrade stops with `ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED` and exit code 1.
Generated: an `@generated` comment at the top of the file, or `linguist-generated` in `.gitattributes`.
Vendored: `linguist-vendored` in `.gitattributes`.
Ignored: a match in `.gitignore` or `.hgignore`.

!     ! src/gen/Gen.tsx - protected by @generated in the leading comment block
ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED: 1 protected file still requires a codemod change:
  src/gen/Gen.tsx — @generated in the leading comment block
Upgrade incomplete: protected changes remain
The upgrade still writes every other file. Its options and exit codes are in `astryx docs cli/commands/upgrade`.
base._title: Authoring › Ship › Upgrading › Know which files upgrades skip

base.name: pick-a-version
base.description: Version your package with semver: a major version for a breaking change, a minor version for a new feature, and a patch for a fix.
prose: Pick a version
Version your package with semver: a major version for a breaking change, a minor version for a new feature, and a patch for a fix.

# 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0: a breaking change
npm version major  # only with npm: npm, which every Node install carries, sets the version
# 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0: a new feature
npm version minor  # only with npm: npm, which every Node install carries, sets the version
# 1.0.0 -> 1.0.1: a fix
npm version patch  # only with npm: npm, which every Node install carries, sets the version
Before 1.0.0, npm treats each minor version as breaking: an app that asks for `^0.6.0` never gets `0.7.0`. Bump the minor version for a breaking change, and the patch for anything else.
Ship a codemod with each breaking change so apps can migrate; see `astryx docs authoring/building-blocks/codemods`.
base._title: Authoring › Ship › Versioning › Pick a version

base.name: know-what-breaks-apps
base.description: A breaking change stops code, commands, or links that worked in an app from working after the upgrade. For an integration, these names are part of its API.
prose: Know what breaks apps
A breaking change stops code, commands, or links that worked in an app from working after the upgrade. For an integration, these names are part of its API.
A component name, such as AcmeCarousel Imports, and astryx component AcmeCarousel
A template id, such as acme-dashboard astryx template acme-dashboard
A theme slug, such as ocean astryx theme add ocean
A topic name or route, such as acme/deploying Reads of the old name, and links to it from other docs
A component's import path Imports written from the old path
An exports entry Imports of that path, which fail with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED
A prop Code that passes it
List each breaking change in your release notes, with the codemod that migrates it. Any changelog tool works. If `package.json` has a `files` allowlist, add `CHANGELOG.md` to it so npm packs it.
base._title: Authoring › Ship › Versioning › Know what breaks apps

base.name: declare-peer-ranges
base.description: Declare the Astryx packages that your code imports as peer dependencies, in `peerDependencies`, so the app installs one copy of each. Keep each range as wide as your tests prove.
prose: Declare peer ranges
Declare the Astryx packages that your code imports as peer dependencies, in `peerDependencies`, so the app installs one copy of each. Keep each range as wide as your tests prove.
@astryxdesign/core Your code imports Core, as a theme does with @astryxdesign/core/theme The Core versions you test, such as ^0.6.0
@astryxdesign/theme-* Your code imports that theme package The versions you test

@astryxdesign/cli You ship a docs section, a placed guide, a template that sets replaces or keywords, a component that sets replaces, a doc section with an id, or a theme >=0.6.6 when you ship a template that sets keywords, >=0.6.7 when a component sets replaces, otherwise >=0.6.4. Optional in peerDependenciesMeta

`integration verify` fails a package that needs the CLI peer and lacks it, or whose range admits a stable CLI too old for what it ships. `integration add doc --parent` and `integration add theme` write the peer for you.

When the CLI is outside that range, `doctor integration validate` and `integration check` list a `cli_peer_version` note naming your package. A note fails nothing, `--strict` included, and `integration verify` does not report it. Below the range the note gives the commands that install a newer Core and CLI together, as dev dependencies in your own package folder, and then run `upgrade --apply`. Above it, in an app the note asks for a release of your package that supports that CLI, and in your own package folder it asks you to test your package with that CLI and widen the range.
base._title: Authoring › Ship › Versioning › Declare peer ranges

base.name: support-older-clis
base.description: An app may run an older CLI than the one you build with. A CLI reads what it knows and skips the rest, but some newer files make an older CLI hide your docs.
prose: Support older CLIs
An app may run an older CLI than the one you build with. A CLI reads what it knows and skips the rest, but some newer files make an older CLI hide your docs.
An unknown field in `astryx.integration.mjs` is ignored with an `unknown_manifest_key` warning, and the rest of the manifest still loads.
A named export that the CLI does not know is ignored with no warning, so `debug` and `gapReport` are safe to add.
Published 0.6.3 and earlier print each `{@link ...}` as written.

Published 0.6.3 and earlier reject a template that sets `replaces` or `keywords`, drop that template, and hide every doc topic your package ships. Published 0.6.4 and 0.6.5 still drop a template that sets `keywords`.
Published 0.6.3 and earlier cannot read a docs section, a section `id`, or a theme folder that `integration add theme` writes. They can then hide every doc topic your package ships.
Published 0.6.2 and 0.6.3 still load your components, but published 0.6.0 and 0.6.1 cannot read the component docs that `integration add component` writes: `component AcmeCarousel` fails there.
An app on an older CLI lists a component whose doc names another export of its file under the file name, and lists no family members, so `component AcmeCarousel` fails there.

`integration verify` requires the CLI peer for a docs section, a placed guide, a template `replaces` or `keywords`, a doc section with an `id`, and a theme. A CLI too old for one of them cannot read it, and when it hides your topics, `docs` gives no warning.

base.name: choose-a-calendar
base.description: `Calendar` shows the Gregorian calendar unless you choose another one. Pass `calendar` to `<InternationalizationProvider>` to set it for a subtree. A locale on its own never changes the calendar: `fa-IR` shows Gregorian dates in Persian…
prose: Choose a calendar

`Calendar` shows the Gregorian calendar unless you choose another one. Pass `calendar` to `<InternationalizationProvider>` to set it for a subtree. A locale on its own never changes the calendar: `fa-IR` shows Gregorian dates in Persian until you pass `calendar="persian"`. A locale with a `-u-ca-` keyword, such as `th-TH-u-ca-buddhist`, keeps Gregorian dates too; set `calendar` to choose one.

Calendar and language are independent: `locale="en" calendar="hebrew"` shows Hebrew dates in English. `Calendar` also takes its own `calendar`, which wins over the provider. Use it when one screen shows two calendars side by side.

Values never change with the calendar. `value`, `defaultValue`, `onChange`, `min`, and `max` stay Gregorian ISO dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) in every calendar, so your data, server code, and existing handlers keep working.
base._title: Internationalization: calendars › Calendar systems › Choose a calendar

base.name: load-temporal-where-the-runtime-lacks-it
keywords: Load Temporal where the runtime lacks it
base.description: Calendars whose months are not Gregorian use the runtime's `Temporal` for their month lengths, leap months, and years. Chrome and Edge 144 and later, Firefox 139 and later, and Node.js 26 and later ship it. Safari and older runtimes do…
prose: Load Temporal where the runtime lacks it

Calendars whose months are not Gregorian use the runtime's `Temporal` for their month lengths, leap months, and years. Chrome and Edge 144 and later, Firefox 139 and later, and Node.js 26 and later ship it. Safari and older runtimes do not. Astryx bundles no polyfill, so Gregorian applications pay nothing.

Where `Temporal` is missing, load the full build of `temporal-polyfill` before your app renders. The default build has no non-ISO calendars. Load it only where `Temporal` is missing: a native implementation is more accurate for the lunisolar calendars.

If you render on the server, load it there too. `Calendar` resolves its calendar during render, so a server without `Temporal` renders Gregorian dates, and a browser with it renders Persian ones: hydration then fails. When both have `Temporal`, or both lack it, they render the same markup.

Without a `Temporal` that supports it, a calendar that needs one shows Gregorian dates and warns once in development, on the server and in the browser. The Gregorian-aligned calendars (`buddhist`, `roc`, `japanese`) work everywhere without it.
titles: Load Temporal where the runtime lacks it
base._title: Internationalization: calendars › Calendar systems › Load Temporal where the runtime lacks it

base.name: lunisolar-calendars
base.description: In the lunisolar calendars, months start on new moons computed from astronomy, and runtimes do not all agree on a few of them. Astryx follows the runtime's `Temporal` and does not correct it.
prose: Lunisolar calendars
In the lunisolar calendars, months start on new moons computed from astronomy, and runtimes do not all agree on a few of them. Astryx follows the runtime's `Temporal` and does not correct it.
Native `Temporal` in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Node.js 26 agrees with official observatory data from 1900 through 2100.

A polyfill reads the platform's `Intl` data instead. Under a polyfill, Node.js 24 starts nine `chinese` and four `dangi` months in that range one day apart from the native result: the first month of the 2027 `chinese` year starts on February 6 with native `Temporal` and on February 7 under the polyfill. Safari uses the same kind of `Intl` data, so expect the same differences there.
Within one browser, the day numbers a person sees, the dates a screen reader announces, and the value they pick agree. Only two different runtimes can disagree.

If you render on the server, a server and a browser that use different implementations can disagree on one of these month starts. The browser then renders that month differently from the server markup, and React renders that part again on the client during hydration. The `temporal-polyfill/full/global` import keeps a native `Temporal` where one exists, so on its own it leaves Chrome, Edge, and Firefox on native `Temporal` and a Node.js 24 server on the polyfill. When identical server and browser markup for these calendars matters more than matching official data, call `installImplementation()` from `temporal-polyfill/full/shim` on the server and in the browser before rendering: it installs the polyfill even over a native `Temporal`. A server runtime with native `Temporal`, such as Node.js 26, also matches native browsers. Otherwise, do not replace a native `Temporal`: that makes native environments less accurate.
base._title: Internationalization: calendars › Calendar systems › Lunisolar calendars

base.name: error-codes
base.description: Stable, append-only machine-readable error codes on the --json error envelope (envelope.code). Codes never change or get removed; branch on these, not on prose.
prose: Error Codes
Stable, append-only machine-readable error codes on the --json error envelope (envelope.code). Codes never change or get removed; branch on these, not on prose.
ERR_UNKNOWN Fallback for any error without a more specific code.
ERR_UNKNOWN_COMMAND A top-level command name was not recognized (e.g. astryx bogus).
ERR_UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND A subcommand under a command group was not recognized (e.g. astryx theme bogus).
ERR_INVALID_OPTION An unknown option was passed, --json was given to a command without JSON output.
ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT An argument or option value is invalid: wrong type, out of range, an unknown choice, an extra argument, or a conflicting combination.
ERR_MISSING_ARGUMENT A required argument or option value was omitted.
ERR_INVALID_LANG --lang was given a value outside its choices (en, zh, dense).
ERR_INVALID_DETAIL --detail was given a value outside its choices (full, compact, brief).
ERR_NODE_VERSION The running Node.js version is below the supported minimum.
ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND @astryxdesign/core could not be located (not installed / not in a monorepo).
ERR_CORE_INCOMPATIBLE The installed @astryxdesign/core loaded but is too old for this input — it lacks a capability the CLI must call to emit correct output (upgrade core).
ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT No component matched the requested name.
ERR_UNKNOWN_HOOK No hook matched the requested name.
ERR_UNKNOWN_TOPIC No docs topic matched the requested name.
ERR_UNKNOWN_SECTION A docs topic exists but the requested section within it does not.
ERR_UNKNOWN_CATEGORY A --category filter value did not match any known category.
ERR_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE No template matched the requested name.
ERR_AMBIGUOUS_TEMPLATE A template id matched more than one template (narrow with --type/--package).
ERR_AMBIGUOUS_COMPONENT A component name is owned by more than one package (narrow with --package).
ERR_AMBIGUOUS_THEME A theme slug is owned by more than one package (narrow with --package).
ERR_UNKNOWN_THEME No theme matched the requested slug (theme add).
ERR_INTEGRATION_ROOT_CONFLICT An integration manifest already declares a different path for the requested contribution root.
ERR_INTEGRATION_EXPORT_CONFLICT A package export already maps a generated contribution subpath to a different target.
ERR_UNKNOWN_PACKAGE No package matched the requested name.
ERR_UNKNOWN_AGENT An unrecognized --agent value was passed to init.
ERR_UNKNOWN_FEATURE An unrecognized --features value was passed to init.
ERR_UNKNOWN_CODEMOD A --codemod value did not match any registered codemod (upgrade).
ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED A codemod or post-codemod hook failed during an upgrade run; the error carries a receipt that lists the files the run already changed.
ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED A required codemod change remains blocked by a protected consumer file.
ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTION_SOURCE A working-tree protection declaration could not be read or parsed.
ERR_NOT_FOUND A generic discover/lookup query matched nothing in any package.
ERR_NO_DOC A component exists but has no typed .doc.mjs file.
ERR_NO_SHOWCASE No showcase exists for the requested component.
ERR_NO_SOURCE No source file could be located for the requested component/template.
ERR_INVALID_DOC A component's docs failed validation (malformed .doc.mjs).
ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND A required input file did not exist.
ERR_FILE_EXISTS Refused to overwrite an existing file.
ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL A path escaped its allowed root, or a name contained traversal markers.
ERR_WRITE_FAILED Writing output files failed (and was rolled back).
ERR_THEME_INVALID A theme definition or contributed theme descriptor is invalid.
ERR_THEME_LOAD A theme file could not be loaded / parsed into a defineTheme result.
ERR_PALETTE_GENERATION A palette generation request or one of its constraints was invalid.
ERR_VERSION_DETECT The current @astryxdesign/core version could not be detected.
ERR_INVALID_VERSION A --from/--to value was not a valid semver string.
ERR_DEP_MISSING A required external dependency (e.g. jscodeshift) is missing.
ERR_GH_CLI GitHub CLI (gh) is not installed or not authenticated.
ERR_UNKNOWN_POST No blog post matched the requested slug in the feed.
ERR_FETCH_FAILED A network fetch (RSS feed or post text) failed.
ERR_LAYOUT_PARSE A layout expression failed to parse (syntax error, with line/col).
ERR_LAYOUT_INVALID A layout expression parsed but failed validation (unknown component/prop/enum/block).
ERR_UNCLASSIFIED_EXIT Recorded in the debug log, never printed: a command exited non-zero without reporting an error code.
ERR_SIGNAL_TERMINATED Recorded in the debug log, never printed: the process was ended by a signal (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM) before the command reached a terminal path.

ERR_VERSIONS_UNAVAILABLE Nothing could answer this run, and nothing was written: the project's own CLI could not start and nothing else could answer, or the Core a command needs outside a project could not be installed.
ERR_PROJECT_REQUIRED The command needs a project (an app with Astryx installed, or an integration package) and was run outside one. Nothing was written.
