base.name: response-types
base.description: The `type` discriminant present on every --json success envelope. Consumers switch on it to narrow `data`.
prose: Response Types
The `type` discriminant present on every --json success envelope. Consumers switch on it to narrow `data`.

init.run The install receipt: the mode (default | features), the features run, agent-doc files written, any soft docsError, whether theme guidance was emitted, the template outcome (workflow | created | skipped) plus its path, and whether the next-steps were emitted.
init.remove The removal receipt — returned when --remove-agents is set: data.removed is true when a managed agent-docs block was found and removed, and false when there was none to remove.

init.user The computer-level agent text receipt — returned when --user is set: data.files, one {path, action, reason?} per path acted on, the skill file first and then each link to its folder (action written | linked | unchanged | removed | absent | kept; reason only on kept: edited when a person changed the text, not-astryx when Astryx did not write it), data.command (the command the text names), and data.warnings.

component.list The component catalog grouped by component group (each component's group field): detail (the level: names | compact | full) and components, the grouped map of names entries ({name, package, and optional canonical import for integrations}), brief entries ({name, package, description, import}), or a full ComponentDoc per entry with its package.

component.batch The component specialization of the shared BatchResponse and BatchRow types. An explicit programmatic selector array, or two or more CLI selectors, returns one ordered receipt: count plus results, one row per selector including duplicates. Every row carries selector and status (found | not_found | ambiguous | error). A found row carries result, the same {type, data} response as one selector. An ambiguous row carries code, error, and candidates ({package, component, kind, installed}). Other failed rows carry code, error, and optional suggestions ({name, reason}).

component.detail One component's authored ComponentDoc plus ownership fields (package, the owner; import, the specifier; sourceAvailable, whether source exists) and parentDoc (present when the component is documented inside another component's doc, naming that doc). The envelope's package names the same owner.
component.detail.props Just one component's props table (ComponentPropDoc[]). The envelope's package names the npm package that owns the component.
component.detail.source One component's source file, as {component, source}. The envelope's package names the npm package that owns the component.
component.detail.showcase One component's showcase example, as {component, aspectRatio, source}. The envelope's package names the npm package that owns the component.

component.detail.blocks One component's example blocks, as {component, showcase, examples, related} of BlockEntry ({name, package, displayName, description, isShowcase, category}); each block names the package that owns it, and the envelope's package names the component's owner.

docs.list All reference-doc topics as DocsListEntry[] ({topic, description, package, replaces?, replacedPackage?}), in read order; meta.namespaces lists the docs tree's top-level namespaces, and meta.notLoaded each package whose docs did not load.

docs.detail One topic's full ReferenceDoc (the JSON read of a topic, --full, --dense, or a topic with one section), with token-ref blocks inlined and each section naming the package that wrote it, plus links ({up, previous, next}: the commands that open the level it sits in and its neighbors there). A topic or guide that took another's place carries replaces and replacedPackage, the package whose topic or guide it replaced.

docs.index One topic's section index, the text read of a topic with more than one section (and --index): the topic's name, title, and description, plus sections, each {id, title, package, summary} (pass the id as the section argument; package is the npm package that wrote the section; summary is the section's one-line summary), and links ({up, previous, next}: the commands that open the level it sits in and its neighbors there); replaces and replacedPackage when the topic or guide took another's place.

docs.detail.section One ReferenceSection of a topic, found by key or title, with token-ref blocks inlined, plus links ({up, previous, next}: the commands that open its topic index and the sections before and after it). The envelope's package names the npm package that wrote the section.

docs.node One node of the docs tree, read by its route: its id, kind, package, title, summary, and breadcrumb, plus a namespace's slots with their children (one level down, each naming its package, and a guide an integration replaced its replaces and replacedPackage) or a typed doc's content, and links ({up, previous, next, related}: the commands that open its parent, its neighbors, and the docs it names).
blog.list The feed URL plus every post parsed from the RSS feed, each with slug, title, description, date, type, authors, link, and plaintext URL.
blog.detail One post's metadata plus the feed URL and the post's full plaintext body.

discover.list What the project has, the integrations it loads and the official packages it declares, official packages first (package, the npm package and always equal to name; name, category, components, version, a list per other kind they add, and latest when a source knows it); meta.available lists what the project could add, the official packages first, each with its package and the command that adds it, and meta.sources reports each source, the official list last; when it lists no integration it carries meta.configured to tell "nothing configured" from "nothing discovered".

discover.detail One package, for an @scope/name or @scope/name@version query: its package (the npm package the result is about), what the shown version adds, whether the project has it, and, when a source knows the package, its versions, latest release, and the command that adds it.
discover.detail.doc The validated ComponentDoc for one installed component, for an @scope/name/Component query, plus package, the npm package that owns the component.

discover.item One item that is not an installed component, for an @scope/name/<item> query: its kind, name, package, version, and whether the project has the package. The envelope's package names the same package.

discover.search The echoed query plus every matching item and package across all packages, each with its kind and whether the project has it, even when only one matches; total is set when --limit cut the list.

search The echoed query, matchCount (total matches, before limit), and results, a ranked SearchResultEntry[] bounded by limit: each {domain, name, package, score, reason, description, command} (package is the npm package that owns the result), plus import (components, hooks), title, parent (the command that opens the level above), and, for a hit on one section, section (docs), or displayName and kind (templates). The result for a deprecated component also carries deprecated {replacement, description}: the name of the component to use instead and the modernization route, from its doc. When a search with no type could not obtain @astryxdesign/core, meta.partial is {skipped, reason}: the domains it skipped (component, hook, template) and why.

build.help The how-to-build-a-page playbook, emitted when no query is given: playbook: true, a title, the ordered steps (title, commands, optional returns), the on-system rules, and related lookups. Commands are bare subcommands for the caller to render with its own invocation.

build.kit The template to start from and its kit: query, hasResults, matchCount (never a cap), directMatch, start {name, package, command, basis, reason, alternatives, ...} (the start and each alternative name the package that owns the template), pages (search's closest templates), blocks and domain as SearchResultEntry[] (each naming its package), frame and foundation (Core component names), and hint {reason, commands} when thin.
swizzle.list The names of swizzlable components discoverable from cwd's @astryxdesign/core. The envelope's package is @astryxdesign/core.

swizzle.copy An eject receipt: component name, owning package, output directory, files-copied count, the copied file names (relative to the component folder; owner modules copied beside it start with ../), whether any file uses StyleX, and, when the owner has an issues URL, feedback ({issuesUrl, ghCommand?}): where to report the gap that led to swizzling. The envelope's package names the same owning package.

gap-report.categories The fixed gap category values and human-readable labels; when a loaded integration names its own issues URL, meta.destinations lists every destination ({to, default, issuesUrl}) and meta.ask tells an agent to ask the person.

gap-report.file An aggregate receipt: overall status, the selected package, issuesUrl (or null), deliveries in handler order, each {handlerType: project | integration | fallback, handler, audience, status, url, message}, and filedCount/routedOnlyCount totals; without --to, when a loaded integration names its own issues URL, destinations and ask as on gap-report.categories.
template.list The effective discovered TemplateListEntry[] for pages and blocks. A winning replacement entry includes optional replaces, naming the Core id omitted from the default list.

template.show The resolved template's source, exactly as a copy writes it, plus its description, kind, the component names it composes, and demoMediaReplaced (how many Astryx demo media references were replaced with placeholders for you to swap for your own media), and demoContentReplaced (how many Astryx docs-only demo content elements were replaced with a Text placeholder for your own content).

template.skeleton A layout skeleton (structural tags with spatial annotations) plus the template's description and the components it composes. The envelope's package names the npm package that owns the template.

template.copy A scaffold receipt: template id, output directory, written file name, file count, demoMediaReplaced (how many Astryx demo media references were replaced with placeholders), demoContentReplaced (how many Astryx docs-only demo content elements were replaced with a Text placeholder), notes (setup notes naming what the template needs that the project lacks — missing packages, missing StyleX compiler; empty when satisfied), missingPackages (external package names the template imports that are not in the project), and installCommand (a ready-to-run install command with the detected package manager and workspace version ranges; null when nothing is missing, or when several lockfiles leave the package manager undetermined). The envelope's package names the npm package that owns the template.

template.cdn A write receipt for the no-build-step CDN starter page: the path (relative to cwd), the Astryx version every CDN URL was pinned to, whether it was written, and the reason it was not. exists when a file was already there, which is a success.

hook.list The hook catalog grouped by category: detail (the level: names | compact | full) and components, the grouped map of hook names, brief entries, or a full HookDoc per entry. The envelope's package is @astryxdesign/core, the only package that ships hooks.
hook.detail One hook's full authored HookDoc. The envelope's package is @astryxdesign/core.
hook.detail.params Just one hook's parameters table (HookParamDoc[]). The envelope's package is @astryxdesign/core.

theme.build A theme build receipt: name, tokenCount and componentCount (override counts), sizeKB, the written outputs {css, cssDts, js, dts, and variantsDts when applicable}, warnings (defects to fix), and notices (advisories about a correct theme, such as a named font it does not load).
theme.build.check The --check receipt: theme name, an upToDate flag, the stale outputs (each {path, reason: missing | outdated}), and the full list of checked paths. Writes nothing.

theme.build.batch Several themes built in one invocation: count plus one {file, receipt} per theme in argument order, where receipt is that theme's theme.build (or theme.build.check) envelope, or null when it produced no CSS.

theme.list Every bundled, installed package, and local theme as a ThemeListEntry[]. Each entry has slug, displayName, description, maintained, owner package or local root, source, added, and default fields. Optional meta.unmigratedCopies names earlier descriptor-less copies, their missing descriptor, and the upgrade command; those copies are not data entries.

theme.app The app theme record after add, remove, or use. It includes every added theme and its built imports, the default slug, generated module path, and the command change. After add, the envelope package names the npm package that owns the added theme; a local theme has none.

theme.eject A local source-fork receipt with the resolved slug, displayName, source theme maintained flag, source-selector package, outputDir, source entry, exportName, and every file written, including the descriptor. The written local descriptor always uses maintained: false.

theme.template A write receipt for the annotated theme template: the path (relative to cwd), whether it was written, and the reason it was not. exists when a file was already there, which is a success.

theme.targets The whole themeable surface: the echoed filter, componentCount, and targets, one per theming target — {key, className, component, props, states}, where props and states are its legal override keys.

theme.palette.generate An author-reviewable OKLCH palette response: recipe (astryx-oklch-v1), status (candidate), familyCount, stopCount, modes, candidate (TonalPaletteCandidate), and generationReceipt. The generationReceipt contains schemaVersion (1), recipe, generatorVersion (palette-generator-v1), candidateFormatVersion (palette-typescript-v1 or palette-json-v1), candidateSha256, optional preview, resolved request, and diagnostics. File-write fields are output, receipt, preview, written, and reason (exists or null).
upgrade.list Every available codemod, oldest→newest, as {name, package, title, version, optional}; returned for --list without running anything.

upgrade.registry The copied-composition receipt for --registry: applied, ok, the counts (found, current, wouldUpdate, updated, wouldMerge, merged, wouldRefreshReceipt, receiptsRefreshed, conflicts, missing, invalid, failed), and items.

upgrade.status A short-circuit outcome with no codemods run (up_to_date, no_codemods, or config_fixable), each carrying the agent-docs summary. no_codemods and config_fixable carry cliBehindCore ({cliVersion, command}) when the installed Core is newer than the CLI, which then has no codemods for the releases after its own version.

upgrade.run The run receipt: from/to versions, codemod count, integrations processed, the agent-docs summary, sourcePathFound (false when the resolved source directory does not exist, so no source file was read), and (apply mode) filesChanged, transformsApplied, and per-codemod errors. regenerate lists generated files to rebuild, each with its codemods, commands and messages. When the installed Core is newer than the CLI, it also carries cliBehindCore ({cliVersion, command}): codemods for the releases after cliVersion did not run.

manifest The CLI capability manifest: name, version, apiVersion, description, globalOptions, commands (each name, description, arguments, options, json, aliases?, responseTypes?, examples?, exitCodes? as [{code, when}], outsideProject? (same, refuse, or own; absent on a group), subcommands?), jsonSupported, globalMode ({docs, summary}: what a run may do beyond its command, such as the hand-off to the project's own CLI, the daily update check, and the agent skill file, and the docs topic that explains it), and the flat responseTypes index.

help Help, in one of two shapes. A bare astryx --json returns the root manifest: name, version, commands (the command names), jsonSupported, and manifest (the full payload astryx manifest --json returns). --help --json on any command, or astryx help [command] --json, returns that command's help: command, description, usage, options (each flags, description, and defaultValue and choices when set), and subcommands (each name and description). data.manifest marks the first shape; data.usage marks the second.
version The CLI version, for astryx --version --json: {version}.
doctor The health-check report: checks (each with id, label, status: pass | warn | fail | info, a message, and an optional fix, always present on warn and fail) plus a summary of counts per status.
integration.add A contribution-writer receipt: kind, name, optional root {path, created}, integration-manifest path, every affected project-relative path, written, and dryRun.

integration.pack-check The packed-package check: name, version, packable, tarball {filename, fileCount, size, unpackedSize} or null, inventory {manifest, roots [{kind, path, expectedFiles, missingFiles, complete}], expectedFiles, packedFiles}, contributions {local, packed}, each null or {themes [{slug, exportName}], components, templates [{id, type, name}], codemods [{version, id}], docs, agentDocsAppend}, and issues [{code, severity, message, fix?, file?, line?}] (the issues validation finds in the source and, prefixed packed_, in the packed tree, with the fix and the place when the check knows them).

integration.validate The validation result: validated (false when nothing was validated: with no package.json the issues list carries one no_package error so the command exits 1, and with a package.json but no integration manifest the issues list is empty and proves nothing), the package name and version (both null when validated is false) plus issues, an AstryxIntegrationIssue[] of {code, severity: warning | error, message, fix?, file?, line?} (fix: the change that resolves it; file and line: where, relative to the package), and notes when there are any: {code, message, next?} information beside the issues (text output marks a next note [next minor]); a note fails nothing by default, and one with next: true counts as a warning under integration check --next, fails integration check --strict --next, and fails --strict from the next minor release. Notes include invalid_cli_command for a malformed cliCommand and cli_peer_version when the running CLI is outside the @astryxdesign/cli peer range of the package, and the package layout findings added after the last minor release, each with its fix in the message (duplicate_component_doc, symlinked_root, unreadable_file, invalid_package_json, no_provider_id, source_without_component_doc where a doc and its source still pair), and doc_name_mismatch and unknown_block_component, until they become warnings in the next minor release. For the commands a topic writes, runner_command (written with a package runner), plain_command (written bare), package_manager_command (written for one package manager) and doc_token (a token that does not parse) notes each give the file, line and the token to write. A doc_target_not_found note names a doc whose replaces or extends names no topic and no guide of the CLI docs or the docs of the package (such as a namespace), and a doc_section_unplaced note a section whose before or after names no section of what it extends (it is added at the end), and a duplicate_guide_replacement note two docs of the package that replace one guide; they become warnings in the next minor release. When the manifest loads, docTypes checks each doc against its published authoring type: status (checked | skipped), reason, typescript, docs, findings (all warnings, each naming the field and a fix), unchecked, and fixtures (test fixture docs not checked). When the manifest loads, docNames lists the component doc names it could not judge: status (checked), findings (always empty; a doc name the module its import names provably does not export is a doc_name_mismatch note, with its fix in the message) and unchecked ({file, name, reason}: a doc whose name differs from the name it is listed under and whose source exports cannot all be read, such as a re-export from another package). When the manifest loads, blockComponents lists the component names templates give in exampleFor or componentsUsed that could not be judged: status (checked), findings (always empty; a name neither the package nor Core has, and the template does not import, is an unknown_block_component note, with its fix in the message) and unchecked ({file, name, reason}: a name the template may reach through anything other than named imports and re-exports from Core, React, StyleX, local helpers or the entry of the package itself, such as an import from another package, a default or namespace import, an alias of or member read off an imported binding, require() or a dynamic import(), or a local module that cannot be read, or any name Core would have to resolve when Core is not installed). Since 0.7.3 each import apps cannot use is also a note (its fix in the message), listed only and failing --strict from the next minor. So are the examples a package ships: component_without_example (a published component no block shows with exampleFor and isShowcase: true, or names in alsoShowcaseFor), template_category (a category written as a path, such as components/X), showcase_not_standalone (a showcase importing server-only code or reading process.env past NODE_ENV) and template_asset_not_packed (a new URL(…, import.meta.url) asset missing, or left out by npm pack --dry-run). When npm cannot list the files, an asset no files entry can reach is still a note and any other is listed in exampleAssets ({status: checked, findings: [], unchecked}, only when it lists any) as {file, asset, reason}. publicImports ({status: checked, findings: [], unchecked}) lists each import the check could not judge as {file, specifier, reason}; never counted or failed on. For the package being authored, olderCliNotes ({file, kind: template | namespace, field, message}) lists each descriptor field a CLI before 0.7.4 refuses, such as stability on a template or namespace doc; it is present only when it has entries, and is never counted or fails a check.

integration.template-conflicts validated (false when no integration manifest was found, so nothing was inspected), the integration identity, structural issues, and non-blocking Core template-id conflicts as {id, severity: warning, integrationPackage, integrationType, integrationName, coreMatches, message, command}.

integration.component-conflicts validated (false when no integration manifest was found, so nothing was inspected), the integration identity, structural issues, and non-blocking conflicts where an integration component name is also owned by Core; each conflict includes the exact package-qualified command. When the manifest loads and declares a components root, propDrift compares documented props with the TypeScript props: status (checked | skipped), reason, typescript, components, typesCompared, typesSkipped, findings (all warnings; a default_mismatch carries docDefault, codeDefault, and a fix), unchecked, typesNotCompared, and propsNotChecked.

integration.doc-conflicts validated (false when no integration manifest was found, so nothing was inspected), the integration identity, structural issues, and Core doc overlaps. Each finding includes severity (info | error) and relationship (replaces | extends | accidental). copiedPassages lists each pair of topics that repeat 10 or more words of prose word for word: topic, section, otherTopic, otherOwner (package | core), words, passages, owner (the topic that should keep the text), text (the passage as the topic writes it), line (where the copy starts in the topic to change, or null), and message (the exact replacement); each is also a copied_passage warning in issues. fluff lists padding phrases and low-density topics: topic, kind (phrase | density), phrase, section, file (relative to the package root), line, density, and message (what to cut or write instead); each is also a doc_fluff warning in issues. strayPointers lists each code span that is exactly astryx docs <name> for a doc that exists, in the prose, description or summary of a topic or the text fields of a component doc: topic (the topic or component doc), kind (topic | component), section, field (the field outside any section, such as description or usage.bestPractices[0].description, else null), file (relative to the package root), line, pointer (the written command), link (the {@link} that replaces it), and message; each is also a stray_doc_pointer warning in issues.

integration.check Every source check of an integration package in one result: validated (false when no integration manifest was found, so nothing was checked), the package name and version, strict, next (true with --next), and checks, one entry per check (validate, components, templates, docs), each with check, errors, warnings, skipped, failed, and response, the envelope that check returns on its own. The totals are errors, warnings, and skipped; unchecked counts what the checks could not compare, and upcoming how many of the validate notes carry next: true. With --next those notes count as warnings in the validate row and the totals. With --strict, failures lists each warning and each piece of skipped work again as an error, in the issue format the checks use, and with --strict --next each next note too; it is empty without --strict. failed decides the exit code.

base.name: assertResponse
base.description: Parse and assert one expected response type, throwing on an error or a mismatch.
prose: assertResponse()
Parse and assert one expected response type, throwing on an error or a mismatch.

The strict alternative to parseResponse + manual narrowing: it parses, rethrows a CLIError as an Error carrying the CLI message, and rejects any envelope whose `type` is not the one you asked for. Use it when a call site expects exactly one response type and any other outcome is a bug worth failing on.
assertResponse(raw: unknown, expectedType: string): any
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/json`.
raw (required) unknown The CLI stdout to parse: a JSON string, or an object that was already parsed.
expectedType (required) string The response discriminant the caller requires (e.g. 'component.detail').
any The parsed envelope, guaranteed at runtime to carry the requested type. The published signature is untyped; cast to the matching *Response type for typed access.
Error a plain Error with no code: the CLI returned an error envelope (its message is rethrown; code and suggestions are dropped), or the response type is not expectedType

Require one type const r = assertResponse(stdout, 'component.detail');
r.data.name; // safe: any other outcome threw

base.name: blog
base.description: List blog posts, or read one, from the published RSS feed.
prose: blog()
List blog posts, or read one, from the published RSS feed.

Reads the design system blog the same way any feed reader does, over the published RSS feed, never the blog's source files. With no slug it lists every post parsed from the feed; with a slug it reads that post's full plaintext body via the .txt alternate the feed advertises. Both envelopes carry feedUrl so a caller can hit the RSS feed directly.
blog(slug?: string): Promise<BlogListResponse | BlogDetailResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
slug string Post slug (matched case-insensitively) to read in full. Omit to list every post.
blog.list The feed URL plus every post parsed from the feed, each with slug, title, description, date, type, authors, link, and its plaintext URL.
blog.detail One post's metadata plus the feed URL and the post's full plaintext body.
ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT the slug is provided but is not a string
ERR_UNKNOWN_POST no post in the feed matches the requested slug
ERR_FETCH_FAILED the RSS feed or post text cannot be fetched (network error, timeout, non-2xx, or oversized), or the post has no plaintext alternate in the feed
List posts const {data} = await blog();
Read one post await blog('introducing-astryx');
`astryx blog` runs it. Read it with `astryx docs cli/commands/blog`.
base._title: Astryx CLI › API › Functions › blog()

base.name: build
base.description: Page-building assistant: the how-to-build playbook, or the page template to start from for an idea.
prose: build()
Page-building assistant: the how-to-build playbook, or the page template to start from for an idea.

The "build a page" entry point. Called with no query it returns the how-to-build-a-page playbook as data: the workflow steps with their commands, the on-system rules, and related lookups. Called with a query it names the page template to START from (always one: the page template a ranker built for long descriptions puts first; for a part of a page, the page it names; else the app shell) and the next two templates, and the unified search grouped around it: the other close page templates, drop-in blocks, and idea-specific components/hooks, plus the always-on frame + foundation. A template carries the page frame and spacing, so the kit never recommends composing a page from components.
build(query?: string, options?: BuildOptions): Promise<BuildHelpResponse | BuildKitResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
query string  What you're building (e.g. "analytics dashboard"). Omit for the how-to-build playbook.
options.cwd string process.cwd() Directory to resolve @astryxdesign/core and templates from.
options.type 'component' | 'hook' | 'doc' | 'template' | 'theme'  Restrict the underlying search to a single domain.
options.limit number 60 Max results pulled from search before grouping into the kit.

build.help Emitted when the query is omitted: the page-building playbook — playbook: true, a title, the ordered steps (each a title, its commands, and optionally what the step returns), the on-system rules, and related lookups. Each command is a bare subcommand ({command, purpose?}) for the caller to render with its own CLI invocation.

build.kit The page template to start from and the kit around it: the echoed query, hasResults/matchCount/directMatch fields, start (the template to scaffold, the template <id> --type page <path> command that selects it, whether the page ranker's pick is also search's direct match, the closest page, or the fallback app shell, the ranker's next two alternatives, and optional notes — setup notes naming what the template needs that the project lacks, such as missing packages or a missing StyleX compiler), search's closest page templates (≤3), drop-in block patterns (≤5), idea-specific components/hooks (≤6), and the always-on frame + foundation component-name arrays. Carries hint only when the kit came back thin — what to try instead, so a caller does not read a near-empty kit as "the package has nothing".
ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT a query is given and options.type is not a known domain, or options.limit is not a positive integer
ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND a query is given and @astryxdesign/core cannot be found from cwd

ERR_VERSIONS_UNAVAILABLE a query is given outside a project, or in a project with nothing installed, and the Core of the release that answers is not beside it or cached, and cannot be installed into the per-user cache (offline, a registry without it, or an unwritable cache)
Get the playbook const r = await build();

Find the template to start from const {data} = await build('analytics dashboard');
// data.start.command: 'astryx template dashboard --type page <path>'
Restrict + limit await build('pricing', {type: 'template', limit: 10});
`astryx build` runs it. Read it with `astryx docs cli/commands/build`.
base._title: Astryx CLI › API › Functions › build()

base.name: component
base.description: Resolve one or several components by name, or list the catalog, with optional focused slices (props, source, showcase, blocks).
prose: component()
Resolve one or several components by name, or list the catalog, with optional focused slices (props, source, showcase, blocks).

Routes on its arguments: one string resolves that component across core and integration packages; an array returns one ordered result row per selector at every array length; and no name returns the catalog grouped by category. Boolean flags narrow each resolved component to just its props, source, showcase, or example blocks. An integration component that replaces a Core component (its doc sets replaces, and its package declares the CLI range that turns replacement on) answers to the Core name in detail, batch, and list results; use options.package '@astryxdesign/core' for the original. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, components from integrations installed next to this CLI package globally resolve too; inside a project, only the project's own integrations count. See `astryx docs global` and `astryx docs global/computer-integrations`.

base.name: discover
base.description: Browse and search integrations: the ones a project has and, through the official list and discover sources, the ones it could add.
prose: discover()
Browse and search integrations: the ones a project has and, through the official list and discover sources, the ones it could add.

Lists the integrations a project loads and the official packages it declares, then the packages it could add: the official Astryx packages first, from the list the CLI carries, then whatever the discover sources of the project and its integrations list, with what each one adds per kind. An @scope/name query shows one package with every version its source knows; @scope/name@version shows one version; @scope/name/Component returns an installed component's validated doc, and any other item path returns that item. A free-text term searches every item and package. Discover only reads: it prints the command that adds a package and never runs it. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, integrations installed next to this CLI package globally are listed as installed; inside a project, only the project's own are, and the compatible global ones are listed in `meta.available` with source `installed for this computer` and an `install` command. See `astryx docs global` and `astryx docs global/computer-integrations`.
discover(query?: string, options?: DiscoverOptions): Promise<DiscoverListResponse | DiscoverDetailResponse | DiscoverDetailDocResponse | DiscoverItemResponse | DiscoverSearchResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
query string  A package (@scope/name, optionally @version), an item path (@scope/name/<item>), or a free-text term. Omit to list packages.

options.components boolean  In the CLI package list, print every component, and every other item, of each package instead of the first 10. A display flag for the CLI renderer; the programmatic response is unchanged.
options.type 'component' | 'template' | 'doc' | 'theme' | 'codemod' | 'agent-doc'  Only one kind: in the list, packages that add it; in a search, items of that kind.
options.installed boolean false Only what the project has. Cannot be set with options.available.
options.available boolean false Only what the project could add. Cannot be set with options.installed.
options.limit number 20 Max number of search results, a positive integer.
options.lang string  Language code to translate a resolved component doc into.
options.zh boolean false Return a resolved component doc in Chinese.

discover.list What the project has: the integrations it loads and the official packages it declares (package, the npm package and always equal to name; name, category, components, version, and a list per other kind they add), official packages first. meta.available lists what the project could add, official packages first, each with its package and the command that adds it; inside a project, an integration installed for the computer that the project does not install is listed there too, with source installed for this computer and the install command for the project in install. meta.sources reports each source, the official list last. When it lists no integration it carries meta.configured.

discover.detail One package: its package (the npm package the result is about), what the shown version adds, whether the project has it, its versions and latest release when a source knows them, and the command that adds it when the project does not have it. An entry from the official list lists the newest release this CLI knows as latest and the project's Core version; its add command pins the project's Core version, else the Core range it declares (quoted), else the latest release. A version or item the official list does not show answers ERR_UNKNOWN_PACKAGE.
discover.detail.doc The validated ComponentDoc for one installed component, for an @scope/name/Component query, plus package, the npm package that owns the component.
discover.item One item that is not an installed component: its kind, name, the package and version that add it, and whether the project has the package. The envelope's package names the same package.

discover.search The query echoed back plus every matching item and package, each with its kind and whether the project has it, even when one name matches exactly or only one item matches; total is set when the limit cut the list.
ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT the query is a non-string value, or a free-text search is run with an empty query
ERR_INVALID_OPTION options.type is not a known kind, options.limit is not a positive integer, or options.installed and options.available are both set
ERR_UNKNOWN_PACKAGE neither the project, the official list, nor any discover source has the package
ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT the item is not in the named package
ERR_NOT_FOUND a free-text term matches nothing, or the requested version is not published
ERR_INVALID_DOC the resolved component's docs fail to load or are malformed
List packages const {data, meta} = await discover();
Browse a package await discover('@acme/ui');
One version await discover('@acme/ui@2.1.0');
Show a component doc await discover('@acme/ui/Button');
Search templates to add await discover('dashboard', {type: 'template', available: true});

base.name: docs
base.description: Read the reference docs: list every topic, one topic's sections, one section, or a whole topic.
prose: docs()
Read the reference docs: list every topic, one topic's sections, one section, or a whole topic.

No topic lists every reference-doc topic; a topic returns its whole ReferenceDoc, and `index: true` returns its section index (each section's key, title, and summary); a topic plus a section returns that one section. Token-ref blocks are inlined in every read, and so is a section's reference block: the doc it includes, then the command that opens that doc. The topic set is the CLI's own docs plus the ones the project's configured integrations contribute, including any topic an integration replaces or extends, so it depends on the cwd. A route opens a node of the docs tree instead: a namespace such as `cli/api` returns its children one level down (`depth` reads as many levels as asked, and `detail` how much of each doc below), a typed doc such as `cli/api/functions/search` returns its content, and a guide the tree places (`authoring/quick-start`) reads like any topic. Every read but the list carries `links`, the commands that move from it: `up` to the level it sits in, `previous` and `next` to its neighbors, and, for a typed doc, `related` to the docs it names (its command or function, and its related docs); `previous` and `next` to the section or node before and after it. Overlay options select localized or dense variants. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, doc topics from integrations installed next to this CLI package globally are listed too; inside a project, only the project's own integrations count. See `astryx docs global` and `astryx docs global/computer-integrations`.
docs(topic?: string, section?: string, options?: DocsOptions): Promise<DocsListResponse | DocsIndexResponse | DocsDetailResponse | DocsDetailSectionResponse | DocsNodeResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

topic string Doc topic to load (e.g. 'principles'), a docs-tree route (e.g. 'cli/api/functions/search'), or the name of one node of the docs tree: its own name (e.g. 'tokens-color'), or its route without the prefix its name repeats (e.g. 'tokens/color'), where exactly one node answers to it. Omit to list all topics.
section string Section to return: its key (from the topic's index), its title, or a unique part of its title (case-insensitive).
options.lang string Language code for localized doc content.
options.zh boolean Shorthand for Chinese (zh) doc content.
options.dense boolean Return the token-efficient dense doc variant. It is written to be read whole, so it returns the whole doc.
options.index boolean Return the topic's section index (each section's key, title, and summary), even for a topic with one section.

options.depth number | 'all' How many levels below a docs-tree namespace to read: 0 for the namespace alone, 1 for its children (the default), 'all' for every level. Where a read stops, a child with docs below it carries childCount. A doc with nothing below it reads the same at any depth. On the topic list, where each namespace otherwise lists alone, it names the docs below each one, as deep as asked; without it the list is unchanged.

options.detail 'brief' | 'compact' | 'full' How much of each doc below the named one a depth read returns: brief (the default) is its identity; compact and full add its text (a guide's sections, a namespace's or typed doc's content). Given alone, it reads one level down. The topic list names each doc below a namespace by its identity whatever the detail.
options.cwd string Project directory whose configured integrations contribute topics. Defaults to process.cwd(); an unreadable config falls back to the CLI's own topics.

docs.list Every reference-doc topic in read order, as DocsListEntry[] ({topic, description, package, replaces?, replacedPackage?}), each readable with docs(topic). meta.namespaces lists the docs tree's top-level namespaces ({topic, description, package}); with depth, each also carries children, the docs below it as a namespace read names them ({topic, description, route, name, package, kind, title, summary, replaces?, replacedPackage?, stability?}), nested the same way to the depth asked for, and childCount where the depth stops on a doc with docs below it. meta.notLoaded names each package whose docs did not load ({package, message}).
docs.detail One topic's full ReferenceDoc, with token-ref and reference blocks inlined, plus links.
docs.index One topic's section index (index: true): {name, title, description, sections: [{id, title, summary}], links}.

docs.detail.section One ReferenceSection of the topic, found by key or title, with token-ref and reference blocks inlined. Asked of a docs-tree namespace, it is the section read of the one guide below the namespace that has the section.

docs.node A namespace or typed doc in the docs tree, read by its route: {id, route, kind, package, title, summary, breadcrumb, slots, content}. A namespace lists each slot's children one level down, or as deep as depth asks, each child carrying its own slots, childCount where the read stops, and its text at compact or full detail; a typed doc carries its content.
ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT depth is not a whole number of levels or 'all'
ERR_INVALID_DETAIL detail is not brief, compact, or full

ERR_UNKNOWN_TOPIC the topic is not a string, or matches no topic, no docs-tree route, and no one node of the docs tree by its own name or by its route without the prefix its name repeats; a name more than one node answers to opens none of them, and the suggestions list them

ERR_UNKNOWN_SECTION a section is requested but is empty, matches no section, or matches more than one; asked of a docs-tree namespace, when no guide below it or more than one has the section (suggestions name those guides); or asked of a typed doc, which has no sections
List topics const r = await docs();
A whole topic await docs('principles');
A topic's sections await docs('principles', undefined, {index: true});
A docs-tree namespace await docs('cli/api');
Every doc below a namespace, one entry each await docs('cli', undefined, {depth: 'all'});
A namespace and everything below it, in full await docs('authoring', undefined, {depth: 'all', detail: 'full'});
One API function await docs('cli/api/functions/search');
A whole guide from the docs tree await docs('authoring/quick-start');
One section by key await docs('spacing', 'scale');
`astryx docs` runs it. Read it with `astryx docs cli/commands/docs`.

base.name: doctor
base.description: Check a project's Astryx setup and get a pass/warn/fail report per check. Use it as a CI gate or before debugging a broken install.
prose: doctor()
Check a project's Astryx setup and get a pass/warn/fail report per check. Use it as a CI gate or before debugging a broken install.

Runs a series of diagnostics: Node version, @astryxdesign/core install and version alignment with the CLI, installed themes and wiring, astryx.config validity, whether every integration astryx.config names loads (a failed one fails the run), integrations linked from package.json without a config entry, core peer dependencies, integration provider identity and contribution issues, agent docs, the detected package manager, and the health of the docs the CLI reads (authoring and CLI docs, the docs tree, doc size), and returns a structured report. Theme checks run when the generated app module exists; without one, doctor reports that the CLI manages no themes and names theme add, and the `themes` check counts a theme as wired when package.json `astryx.theme` names one or when the source of the app (JavaScript, TypeScript and CSS files, outside dependencies and build output; type-only imports do not count) imports the built module or stylesheet of a discovered theme, the same imports theme add writes, or passes one to Theme (followed through module-scope variables, defineTheme extends, re-exports and installed packages; only a theme whose package is installed, or a local theme, counts), naming the file; a theme passed to Theme that cannot be traced, such as a prop or a variable declared inside a component, is reported as unconfirmed (info), not as missing. Earlier descriptor-less copies are a non-failing upgrade warning. It never installs, writes, or mutates. It imports astryx.config, executes every added theme source while validating private inputs, and loads every recorded built theme module to prove its runtime imports work, including themes from installed packages. Local theme source also runs during build-freshness checks. Stylesheets are parsed without execution. Config and theme top-level code therefore run, so use doctor only with project code you trust. Outside a project it checks the computer instead: the Node version (`node-version`), the release that answered (`answering-release`), the newest release the computer knows of (`newest-release`), the astryx commands on the search path (`cli-on-path`), the integrations installed for the computer (`computer-integrations`: each one used outside a project, and a warning for one skipped because its peer range excludes the answering release or that fails to load), and the computer-level agent text (`computer-agent-text`): present and matching this release, present but different, edited, absent, or turned off, and where it is linked, with `astryx init --user` as the fix for the stale and absent cases. The agent-text check is always info. The newest-release check also runs inside a project: it names a newer release when the computer knows of one; inside a project whose release is older it names the install and upgrade commands; outside one, when the CLI installed for the computer is older, it names the command of the package manager that installed it, after the Node the newest release needs when the computer runs an older one. It is always info and installs nothing. The `cli-on-path` check also runs inside a project: it lists every astryx command on the search path in order, passes when the first is a release that hands each project run to the release of that project, and warns when the first is another program or a release that predates the hand-off, naming `npm install -g @astryxdesign/cli@latest`. Inside a project, `computer-integrations` lists, as info, the integrations installed for the computer that the project does not install, with its install command; they are not used there. It never fails a check because the folder has no project, and installs nothing. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, it checks the computer instead (the Node version, the version that answered, the newest version it knows of, the astryx commands on the search path, the integrations installed globally, and the agent guide for the computer) and never fails a check because the folder has no project. See `astryx docs global` and `astryx docs global/who-answers`.
doctor(options?: DoctorOptions): Promise<DoctorResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
options.cwd string process.cwd() Directory to diagnose. A directory outside any project, a missing one included, gets the computer checks.

options.built string  A finished build to check before you deliver it: a project folder, a build output folder, or one built .html file, relative to cwd. Adds two checks after the others. built-astryx-usage fails when the path holds no value import from an Astryx package (any @astryxdesign/* package or an integration the project installs), no component imported from one, and no Astryx styles in built CSS or HTML. built-astryx-purity warns with the source check of astryx docs is-my-code-good: raw elements Astryx has a component for, raw SVG and icon-library icons, inline styles, classes, stylex.create and imported stylesheets, each with its file and line, in .tsx and .jsx files and JSX in .js source, found by parsing it; it is info, not inspected, when the path holds no source with JSX, such as a bundle. It reads at most 20,000 files, each up to 5 MB, skipping installs and version control; when either limit leaves source unread and nothing was found, the purity check is info, not fully inspected, and when the file limit ends the read before any Astryx turns up, built-astryx-usage warns that the rest went unread instead of failing. Given one built .html file, it also reads the local stylesheets and scripts that page links, finding a root-relative link from the nearest folder above the page that holds it; a linked file that is not there makes built-astryx-usage warn instead of fail. An empty folder fails with nothing checked, like a missing path. A source tree counts as using Astryx through an import, a re-export (export … from) or a stylesheet @import of an Astryx package; a type-only import or re-export (import type, export type, or a list whose names are all type) does not count, since the build erases it. --built goes with doctor alone; a doctor integration check refuses it. A path that does not exist fails built-astryx-usage with nothing checked, and the purity check is left out. The integrations that count are the dependencies the nearest package.json above the path declares whose installed copy, found the way the CLI autolinks (a hoisted workspace copy included), has an integration manifest. The files under the path, and that configuration, are only read, never run. Without it, doctor runs exactly as before.

doctor The diagnostic report: data.checks, each with a stable id, label, status (pass | warn | fail | info), a one-line message, and an optional fix (always present on warn and fail; some info checks carry one too); plus data.summary with counts per status.

Fail a CI step on any failed check const r = await doctor();
if (r.data.summary.fail > 0) process.exitCode = 1;
Diagnose a directory await doctor({cwd: '/path/to/app'});

Check a finished build before delivering it const r = await doctor({built: 'dist'});
if (r.data.summary.fail > 0) throw new Error('Not built with Astryx');
`astryx doctor` runs it. Read it with `astryx docs cli/commands/doctor`.

base.name: gapReport
base.description: Report a missing or hard-to-use design-system capability to the package that owns it.
prose: gapReport()
Report a missing or hard-to-use design-system capability to the package that owns it.

Routes the report to the package that owns the gap: options.package when given, else the integration whose component replaces the named Core component, else the one package that provides the component, else Core. Sends a gap report to every configured handler: the project config handler first, then each integration handler in config order. Each handler has 30 s to finish, and its output goes to stderr. Public handlers run only with confirmPublic; internal handlers always run. With no handler, it files a GitHub issue for the owning package only with confirmPublic (without it nothing is sent), or returns the package's issues URL when that is not on GitHub. With options.to, the report goes only to that integration's issues URL instead, under the same confirmPublic rule. When loaded integrations name their own issues URLs, the response lists every destination with a line telling an agent to ask the person where to file; pass their choice as options.to, never a package the agent picked itself. The report records whether an agent or a person ran it, and the response lists each handler outcome in order.
gapReport(component: string | undefined, options?: GapReportOptions): Promise<GapReportCategoriesResponse | GapReportReceiptResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
component string  Component or general design-system area, up to 120 characters. Required unless listCategories is true.
options.category GapReportCategory  Fixed category from the reported category vocabulary. Required unless listCategories is true.
options.reason string  What capability was missing or difficult, up to 2000 characters. Required unless listCategories is true.
options.detail string  Optional additional context (up to 8000 characters).

options.package string  Package that owns the gap: @astryxdesign/core, or a loaded integration by package name or config entry. Overrides automatic owner routing, which picks the integration whose component replaces the named Core component, else the one package that provides it, else Core; required when more than one package provides the component.
options.confirmPublic boolean false Allow public delivery: public handlers run, and a GitHub issues URL gets an issue filed through the gh CLI.
options.to string  A destination the person chose: a loaded integration whose manifest names an issues URL. The report goes only to that issues URL; handlers do not run.

options.listCategories boolean false Return categories, and the destinations in meta when there is more than one, without resolving a route or writing; the component and every other option are refused with ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT.
options.cwd string process.cwd() Directory used to load project config and component ownership.
gap-report.categories The fixed category values and labels.

gap-report.file Receipt: status (filed, partial, failed, routed_only, consent_required, skipped), package, issuesUrl, ordered deliveries (handlerType, handler, audience, status, url, message), filedCount, and routedOnlyCount.
ERR_MISSING_ARGUMENT component, category, or reason is missing, blank, or not a string (unless listCategories is true)
ERR_UNKNOWN_CATEGORY category is not one of the fixed gap-report values
ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT component is over 120 characters, category is over 80, reason is over 2000, or detail is not a string or is over 8000 characters
ERR_AMBIGUOUS_COMPONENT more than one package owns the named component
ERR_UNKNOWN_PACKAGE the explicitly selected package is not loaded, or options.to names no destination (the error lists the destinations)
ERR_NOT_FOUND no report handler is configured and the owning package has no issues URL
List categories const categories = await gapReport(undefined, {listCategories: true});
Route without public mutation const receipt = await gapReport('Button', {category: 'missing_variant', reason: 'Need a compact size'});
Name the owning package const receipt = await gapReport('Button', {category: 'docs_gap', reason: 'Missing keyboard example', package: '@astryxdesign/core'});

base.name: generateTonalPalette
base.description: Generate candidate tonal palette data without filesystem effects.
prose: generateTonalPalette()
Generate candidate tonal palette data without filesystem effects.

Runs the versioned astryx-oklch-v1 authoring recipe. The returned candidate contains exact hex values for review; it does not modify a theme, write files, perform semantic mapping, or make accessibility claims. Stop numbers remain stable across layouts, and requested decimal stops are emitted explicitly. Anchor policies are intentional: exact preserves the chosen color at its stop; bounded permits movement within maxDeltaE; flexible treats it as guidance. An anchor needs a mode and stop. Stops apply to every family in one request. The candidate always exposes standalone black and white values for direct theme authoring. Generated TypeScript exports them as `black` and `white`, so they can be assigned directly to semantic theme tokens. Those names are reserved and cannot be used as tonal family IDs. The default 0–100 layout also repeats them as family endpoints; a custom stop list can omit those repeated endpoints.
generateTonalPalette(input: TonalPaletteGenerationInput): TonalPaletteCandidate
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
input (required) TonalPaletteGenerationInput Families and seeds plus optional modes, shared stops, anchors, vibrancy from 0 to 100 (default 50), and neutral profile.
TonalPaletteCandidate Deterministic candidate data for author review, including a stops array that defines ramp iteration order and standalone black and white values outside the tonal families.
Error the request, family, seed, stop layout, mode, or anchor is invalid
Generate one family generateTonalPalette({families: [{id: 'blue', seed: '#0074e2'}]});
Preserve a required brand color generateTonalPalette({stops: [50], families: [{id: 'brand', seed: '#0074e2', anchors: [{mode: 'light', stop: 50, color: '#1682d5', policy: 'exact'}]}]});
Allow limited anchor movement generateTonalPalette({stops: [50], families: [{id: 'brand', seed: '#0074e2', anchors: [{mode: 'light', stop: 50, color: '#1682d5', policy: 'bounded', maxDeltaE: 2}]}]});
Use an anchor as guidance generateTonalPalette({stops: [50], families: [{id: 'pink', seed: '#ff4db8', anchors: [{mode: 'light', stop: 50, color: '#ff4db8', policy: 'flexible'}]}]});
Generate an optional accent family generateTonalPalette({families: [{id: 'accent', seed: '#ff4db8'}]});
Generate an explicit intermediate stop generateTonalPalette({stops: [12.5, 50], families: [{id: 'blue', seed: '#0074e2'}]});

base.name: hook
base.description: Resolve a hook by name, or list the catalog, with an optional params-only slice.
prose: hook()
Resolve a hook by name, or list the catalog, with an optional params-only slice.

Routes on its arguments: a name returns that hook's full authored HookDoc; no name (or `list`/`category`) returns the catalog grouped by category. The `params` flag narrows a single hook to just its parameters table.
hook(name?: string, options?: HookOptions): Promise<HookListResponse | HookDetailResponse | HookDetailParamsResponse>

base.name: init
base.description: Non-interactive project setup: install agent docs and point at the theme + build workflows.
prose: init()
Non-interactive project setup: install agent docs and point at the theme + build workflows.

Sets a project up with NO prompts, so it behaves identically for humans, agents, CI, and piped I/O. By default it writes the agent-docs cheat sheet, including guidance from configured integrations, at the project root (the nearest package.json that declares an @astryxdesign package, else the nearest package.json, searching no higher than the repository root): to AGENTS.md, to the project's Claude Code file (CLAUDE.md, else .claude/CLAUDE.md; when CLAUDE.md exists, a block in .claude/CLAUDE.md is removed, unless the project ignores CLAUDE.md, in which case a .claude/CLAUDE.md the project commits keeps a copy), and as a one-line import of AGENTS.md in GEMINI.md unless GEMINI.md already imports it. In the home folder, or in a settings folder in it outside a project, it writes none: every folder of the home folder whose name starts with a dot is a settings folder, and such a folder itself never counts as a project, even with a package.json; a folder below it with a package.json does. The managed block is Astryx-owned: it is written, refreshed, and removed whatever ignore rules or generated markers say, and the text around it is never changed. It then prints getting-started guidance; `features` / `all` print only the chosen features' guidance instead (the theme feature also writes the annotated theme template). With `removeAgents` it removes the managed agent-docs block, at the project root and in `ctx.cwd`, instead of installing. Outside a project it writes the same files but prints no getting-started steps and no step that adds a theme to an app, since those set up a project the folder does not have. With `user` it sets up the computer instead of the folder: it writes the computer-level agent text, one skill file at `~/.agents/skills/astryx/SKILL.md`, linked into the skill folders of agents that read only their own (`~/.claude/skills` always; Kiro, Windsurf, Letta, Xcode's coding assistant, and `~/.config/agents/skills` when that folder exists), with a managed copy for Continue, whose scanner skips links,, telling agents anywhere on the computer that Astryx is there and when to use it; with `user` and `removeAgents` it removes the file and the links it made and records that the text is turned off. The CLI installed for the computer refreshes the file in the background after each upgrade; package install scripts, project setup, and upgrade never write it. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, it writes the agent docs and prints no getting-started steps; `user` writes only the agent guide for the computer, in the home folder, and touches nothing in `cwd`. See `astryx docs global` and `astryx docs global/computer-agent-guide`.
init(options?: InitOptions, ctx?: {cwd?: string}): Promise<InitRunResponse | InitRemoveResponse | InitUserResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.

options.features string  Comma-separated features to install: agents (agent docs), theme (writes the annotated theme.template.ts), template (the page-building commands; writes a page only with templateName).
options.all boolean  Install all features (agents, theme, template).
options.removeAgents boolean  Remove the managed agent-docs block, at the project root and in ctx.cwd, instead of installing. With user, remove the computer-level agent text instead.

options.user boolean  Write or refresh the computer-level agent text instead of setting up ctx.cwd: one skill file at ~/.agents/skills/astryx/SKILL.md in the current user's home folder, linked (a folder symlink with a relative target, a junction on Windows, or a copy where neither can be made) into ~/.claude/skills/astryx, and into the skills folder of Kiro, Windsurf, Letta, Xcode's coding assistant, and ~/.config/agents/skills when that folder exists; Continue, whose scanner skips links, gets a managed copy, refreshed with the file. The text uses the astryx command, or the command of the host that started the run; an integration's cliCommand never applies. Records the links it made, or with removeAgents that the text is turned off, in astryx/settings.json in the per-user configuration folder. A file without the Astryx markers, one edited since Astryx wrote it, or a symlink, is kept as it is, and so is anything at a link target that Astryx did not create. When no astryx command on the computer runs the Astryx CLI, the text is still written and the receipt carries a warning to install the CLI for the computer (npm i -g @astryxdesign/cli). Cannot be combined with features, all, agent, or agentDocsPath.

options.agent string  Agent preset: claude, cursor, codex, hermes, muse, all. all writes every existing agent doc except GEMINI.md, which keeps its one-line import of AGENTS.md. With claude and all, when CLAUDE.md gets the block, a block in .claude/CLAUDE.md is removed, unless the project ignores CLAUDE.md, in which case a .claude/CLAUDE.md the project commits gets a copy too. Used only when the agents feature runs. Refused with user.
options.agentDocsPath string | string[]  Explicit agent-docs file path(s) to write.

options.templateName string  Scaffold this page template to src/pages/<name>/page.tsx. Used only when the template feature runs (features includes template, or all); otherwise ignored. Programmatic only; the CLI never sets it.
ctx.cwd string process.cwd() Directory to set up.

init.run The install receipt: the mode (default | features), the features run, agent-doc files written, any soft docsError, the theme-template outcome (created | skipped | failed) plus its path, the page-template outcome (workflow | created | skipped) plus its path, and whether the next-steps were emitted (never outside a project).
init.remove The removal receipt, returned when removeAgents is set: data.removed is true when a managed agent-docs block was found and removed, and false when there was none to remove.

init.user The computer-level agent text receipt, returned when user is set: data.files, one {path, action, reason?} per path acted on (~/.agents/skills/astryx/SKILL.md, then each link to its folder, such as ~/.claude/skills/astryx; action written | linked | unchanged | removed | absent | kept; reason on kept: edited | not-astryx), data.command (the command the text names), and data.warnings.

ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT --remove-agents is combined with --features, --all, --agent, or --agent-docs-path; --user is combined with --features, --all, --agent, or --agent-docs-path; or --all is combined with --features
ERR_UNKNOWN_AGENT the agents feature runs (default mode, features includes agents, or all) and agent is not one of claude, cursor, codex, hermes, muse, all
ERR_UNKNOWN_FEATURE features contains a name other than agents, theme, or template
ERR_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE the template feature runs and templateName matches no bundled template
ERR_FILE_EXISTS scaffolding a template would overwrite an existing page.tsx

ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL the template output path resolves outside cwd (for example through a symlinked src directory), or, with removeAgents, a managed agent-docs file in cwd, or at the project root when run there, resolves outside that folder through a symlink (run below the root, a project-root file is left as it is with a note)
Default setup const r = await init();
All features await init({all: true});
Remove agent docs await init({removeAgents: true});

Agent text for the whole computer const r = await init({user: true});
for (const w of r.data.warnings) console.warn(w);
`astryx init` runs it. Read it with `astryx docs cli/commands/init`.

base.name: integrationCheck
base.description: Run every source check against the integration package in the current folder, as its build does: validate, components, templates, and docs.
prose: integrationCheck()
Run every source check against the integration package in the current folder, as its build does: validate, components, templates, and docs.

Runs `validateIntegration`, `integrationComponentConflicts`, `integrationTemplateConflicts`, and `integrationDocConflicts` against the integration package in `options.cwd`, and counts each result the way that check's own subcommand exits. The run fails when any of the four would fail on its own. With `strict` it also fails on any warning and on any check that did not run: a package with no integration manifest, or a comparison a check carries that was skipped, such as one that needs the project's TypeScript. `strict` adds no check: it reports those warnings and skipped work again, as errors in the checks' own issue format. A new check, or a new failure code, joins only in a minor release, named in the release notes.
integrationCheck(options?: IntegrationCheckOptions): Promise<IntegrationCheckCommandResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
options.cwd string process.cwd() The integration package folder to check.

options.strict boolean false Also fail on any warning and on any check that did not run, not only on errors. A malformed cliCommand is reported as a note (invalid_cli_command) in data.notes of the validate check, which fails nothing until a minor release names it.
options.next boolean false Also count the findings the next minor release turns into warnings, validate's notes marked next, as warnings now, so strict fails on them.

integration.check data.validated (false when no integration manifest was found, so nothing was checked), data.name and data.version of the package, data.strict, data.next, and data.checks, one entry per check in the order they run (validate, components, templates, docs), each with check, errors (what makes that check's own subcommand exit 1), warnings, skipped (why work did not run), failed (whether that subcommand exits 1), and response, the envelope the check returns on its own. The totals are data.errors, data.warnings, and data.skipped (each reason prefixed with its check); an issue every check starts from, such as one about the manifest, counts once, and every other finding counts on its own. data.unchecked counts the items the checks list as not compared, which never fail it. data.upcoming counts the findings the next minor release turns into warnings (validate's notes marked next), and data.next says whether this run counted them as warnings now. With strict, data.failures lists each warning and each piece of skipped work once again as an error in the checks' own issue format ({check, severity: error, code, message, component, prop, fix, file, line}, each where it applies); it is empty without strict. data.failed decides the exit code.
Check the local package const r = await integrationCheck();

Fail on warnings too const {data} = await integrationCheck({strict: true});
if (data.failed) process.exitCode = 1;
`astryx integration check` runs it. Read it with `astryx docs cli/commands/integration-check`.

base.name: integrationComponentConflicts
base.description: Check integration component names, replaces declarations, and documented props.
prose: integrationComponentConflicts()
Check integration component names, replaces declarations, and documented props.

Loads one local or installed integration, compares its component names with Core, and returns non-blocking conflicts with the exact package-qualified component command required to keep an intentional overlap. Each component's replaces is checked too: its findings are issues, errors for a package that declares the CLI range that turns replacement on and warnings otherwise. A `{@link}` in a component doc's text that names no doc is an `invalid_doc_graph` warning, since it prints as written. Each component doc's props are compared with the component's TypeScript props, read with the project's own `typescript` (or, where `typescript` is missing or has no JavaScript compiler API, as TypeScript 7 does, the `@typescript/typescript6` it installs): a documented prop the code lacks, a prop the package declares that the doc omits, a wrong `required`, or a type that does not match. A type is judged only when it reads exactly: the same text as the source, once whitespace, quotes and union order are set aside (exactly, if it contains `readonly`), or primitives, literals, arrays and unions of those, or a name for one, on both sides, a field such as `status.type` included, and for a union of props types, the type of any one member. A field the prop's variants give different types is listed when the doc gives only some variants' types. A mutable array type matches a readonly one, because callers can pass it; a readonly one documented for a mutable array is a mismatch. `Name = …` with a union after it must match in both parts; one value after it (`Size = 'md'`) is read as a default. A name only TypeScript's own libraries declare is not resolved, and `React.X` resolves through React where the prop is declared. Every other type is listed as not compared, never reported, and so is a name an index signature takes unless exactly one the package declares takes it; with a TypeScript older than 4.8 no type is judged. Those findings are warnings in `propDrift`; without TypeScript it is `skipped` with a reason.
integrationComponentConflicts(pkg?: string, options?: IntegrationAuthoringOptions): Promise<IntegrationComponentConflictResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
pkg string Installed package; omit for the local package.
options.cwd string Resolution directory.

integration.component-conflicts validated (false when no integration manifest was found, so nothing was inspected), integration identity, structural and replaces issues, and Core component-name conflicts with package-qualified commands. An active replacement that keeps the Core name it replaces is not a conflict. When the manifest loads and declares a components root, propDrift holds the props comparison: status (checked | skipped), reason when skipped, typescript, components compared, typesCompared (documented prop types judged), typesSkipped (why none was, with a TypeScript older than 4.8), findings ({component, prop, kind: not_in_code | not_in_doc | required_mismatch | type_mismatch | default_mismatch, severity: warning, message, doc, source, docType?, codeType?, docRequired?, codeRequired?, docDefault?, codeDefault?, fix?}), unchecked ({component, doc, reason}), typesNotCompared ({component, doc, reason, props}: every other documented prop type, grouped by why it was not judged: not a form the check judges exactly (a doc type that does not parse, or a prop a mapped type builds from keys the check cannot trace, included), a field the prop's variants give different types, a standard prop such as className, or a prop declared outside the package), and propsNotChecked when a mapped type builds props from keys the check cannot trace to the package ({component, doc, reason, props}: no warning is drawn for those props).
Check the local integration await integrationComponentConflicts();
`astryx doctor integration components` runs it. Read it with `astryx docs cli/commands/doctor-integration-components`.

base.name: integrationDocConflicts
base.description: Check an integration's docs: the docs tree they add, every link, and overlaps with Core topics.
prose: integrationDocConflicts()
Check an integration's docs: the docs tree they add, every link, and overlaps with Core topics.

Loads one local or installed integration and classifies Core doc overlaps as intentional replacements, intentional extensions, or accidental same-name conflicts that need an explicit relationship or a rename. `copiedPassages` lists each pair of topics that repeat 10 or more words of prose word for word: two of the package's topics, or one of them and a Core topic other than the one it replaces. Code and examples are not compared. `fluff` lists each padding phrase, with its file line, and each topic of 80 or more prose words in which fewer than half carry content. `strayPointers` lists each code span that is exactly `astryx docs <name>` for a doc that exists, in a topic's prose, description or summary or a component doc's text fields, with the `{@link}` that replaces it. Each entry of these lists is also a warning (`copied_passage`, `doc_fluff`, `stray_doc_pointer`), so `integration check --strict` fails on it; the check itself still fails only on errors.

base.name: isError
base.description: Did the CLI return an error envelope?
prose: isError()
Did the CLI return an error envelope?

Tests a parsed response for an `error` key. Branch on this before touching `data`, and prefer the stable `code` field over matching the human-readable message, which is not a contract. Note this returns a plain boolean, not a TypeScript type predicate, so it does not narrow on its own: cast to the matching *Response type to get typed access.
