base.name: search
base.description: Unified ranked search across components, hooks, docs, templates, and themes.
prose: search()
Unified ranked search across components, hooks, docs, templates, and themes.

The single "I'm looking for X" entry point across every content domain. Matching and scores are keyword + fuzzy (not embeddings). Between score bands results keep the lexical order, whose domain priority can put a weaker component, hook, template, or theme above a stronger doc, and a query that is an entry's exact name answers with that entry first. Inside a band, fixed weights order the matches, so a description match can lead a keyword match in the same band (55–99 holds both). A component's usage guidance (its best practices) is indexed one tier below its description, so the words a reader types still find it. In global mode: with `cwd` outside a project, items from integrations installed next to this CLI package globally are searched too, and theme results name no step that adds a theme to an app; inside a project, only the project's own integrations count. See `astryx docs global` and `astryx docs global/computer-integrations`.
search(query: string, options?: SearchOptions): Promise<SearchResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
query (required) string  Free-text search term.
options.type 'component' | 'hook' | 'doc' | 'template' | 'theme'  Restrict results to a single domain.
options.limit number 20 Maximum number of results.

options.cwd string  Directory to resolve @astryxdesign/core from: the project's installed Core, else, outside a project or in a project with nothing installed, the Core of the release that answers, installed into the per-user cache first when needed. A docs-only or themes-only search (type: 'doc' or type: 'theme') does not need it. A search with no type covers the docs and themes alone only when that Core cannot be obtained, and then says so in meta.partial.

search The query echoed back, matchCount (how many candidates matched in total, before limit), plus a ranked SearchResultEntry[] bounded by limit: each has domain, name, score, reason, description, and follow-up command, plus import for components and hooks, title for docs, displayName and kind for templates, and displayName for themes. A deprecated component's result also carries deprecated, {replacement, description} from its doc: the name of the component to use instead and the modernization route. A doc result is the smallest part that answers: one section (with section, and a command that reads only it), one docs-tree route, or a topic, whose command lists its sections. parent is the command that opens the level above it: the section list of its topic, the namespace a tree node sits in, the topic level (Guides or Foundations) for a flat topic, or the topic list for a top-level namespace. Every doc result also carries package, the npm package that authored it (for a section, the package its file came from). A theme result is one theme you can import: name is its slug, its command is astryx theme add <slug> (outside a project, where there is no app to add it to, astryx theme eject <slug>), and package is the npm package that ships it (@astryxdesign/cli for the CLI's own themes). When a search with no type could not obtain @astryxdesign/core, meta.partial is {skipped, reason}: the domains it skipped (component, hook, template) and why; the results are the docs and themes, and text mode prints one line on standard error.
ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT the query is empty, --type is unknown, or --limit is not a positive integer
ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND @astryxdesign/core cannot be found from the cwd, and type names a domain that reads it: component, hook, or template

base.name: swizzle
base.description: Eject a component's source into your project for customization.
prose: swizzle()
Eject a component's source into your project for customization.

Ejects a component's source into the consumer project for deep customization. It copies from the locally resolved @astryxdesign/core (or the owning integration) package source. Every import in the copy names a file the copy holds or a path the owner package exports: names the package exports are imported from its public paths, and every internal module the component needs is copied beside it in the package's folder layout. Tests, stories and docs are not copied. An output folder swizzle owns (one the copy creates, an empty one, or one it marked before) gets an astryx-swizzle.json marker naming each package its copies came from, with its version, so @astryxdesign/build's Babel, PostCSS and Vite integrations, and withAstryx() under webpack, compile the copy below the theme. The receipt flags whether any copied file uses StyleX and lists each npm package the copy imports with the range the owner package declares. With no name (or list) it returns the swizzlable component names instead. An integration component that replaces a Core component is what that Core name copies; options.package '@astryxdesign/core' copies the original. The list names Core components, including one an integration component replaces.
swizzle(component?: string, options?: SwizzleOptions): Promise<SwizzleListResponse | SwizzleCopyResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
component string  Component name to copy (e.g. 'Button'). Omit to list the swizzlable components.
options.cwd string process.cwd() Directory to resolve @astryxdesign/core from.
options.output string './components/astryx' Output directory, relative to cwd. An absolute path, or one that resolves outside cwd, throws ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL.
options.package string  Owning package to copy from when the name is provided by more than one. Use '@astryxdesign/core' to copy an original replaced by an integration component.
options.list boolean false Force the list response even when a component argument is given.

options.overwrite boolean false Replace the component's existing files instead of erroring. A helper an earlier swizzle wrote is never replaced by a copy that carries it: a different one stays, and the new copy writes its own under a version-suffixed name. Swizzling the component whose folder holds that helper counts it as one of that component's own files. A changed private attribute owner module, or a style module it imports, throws ERR_FILE_EXISTS without overwrite and is replaced with it.

swizzle.copy A receipt after copying the component into the project: the component name, owning package, output directory, files-copied count, the copied file names (relative to the component folder; the internal modules copied beside it start with ../, e.g. ../InputGroup/groupStyles.ts), whether any file uses StyleX, the npm packages the copy imports with the ranges the owner declares (dependencies), the output folder's astryx-swizzle.json (marker: {path, written, found?}; written is false for a folder swizzle does not own, and found names up to five entries it already holds), and, when the owner has an issues URL, feedback ({issuesUrl, ghCommand?}): where to report the gap that led to swizzling.

base.name: themeBuild
base.description: Compile a defineTheme() file to scoped CSS, a JS module, and type declarations, or check committed outputs for drift in CI.
prose: themeBuild()
Compile a defineTheme() file to scoped CSS, a JS module, and type declarations, or check committed outputs for drift in CI.

The compiler behind `astryx theme build`. Reads a file that calls defineTheme() and writes a scoped CSS file, a JS module that re-exports the built theme, and a .d.ts (plus an optional .variants.d.ts when the theme adds custom prop values). It uses @astryxdesign/core's own generator, so the CSS matches what the <Theme> runtime emits. When another build step emits the icon registry, {iconsSpecifier} declares the fully specified module path for the generated JS import. Real registry imports are preserved, including aliases, default imports, and namespace imports. Icons inherited through extends are retained, with child entries taking precedence. Comment and string contents do not affect import detection. An inline registry that cannot be preserved fails with ERR_THEME_INVALID before any output is written, including in check mode. Move the registry to its own module and import it into the theme file. With {check: true} it writes nothing and instead compares each output against disk, returning the drift: the CI guard for committed, generated theme CSS.
themeBuild(file: string, options?: {out?: string, check?: boolean, iconsSpecifier?: string}, ctx?: {cwd?: string}): Promise<ThemeBuildResponse | ThemeBuildCheckResponse | null>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
file (required) string  Path to a theme file that calls defineTheme(), resolved against cwd.

options.out string  Override the output CSS path, relative or absolute; a build refuses a path outside cwd, and check mode refuses only a relative path that escapes cwd. The .js, .d.ts and any .variants.d.ts are written in the same directory, named after the theme (<name>.js), not after the CSS file.

options.check boolean false Compile in memory and compare each output against what is on disk instead of writing: the CI drift guard. Because it writes nothing, it also compares outputs outside cwd; when those are stale, the report names the directory that contains them and the build and check commands to run from there, since a build refuses them and each output records the directory it was built from.

options.iconsSpecifier string  Override the selected icon-registry import specifier in the generated JS module, for example ./icons.mjs. With child and inherited registries, this changes the child registry import. When omitted, direct source specifiers are preserved; relative imports followed through a local base are rebased to the theme file. A registry inherited through a package theme must be imported directly to use this option.

ctx.cwd string process.cwd() Directory the theme file, a relative out path, and the returned output paths resolve against. Every output a build writes is inside it, including the default outputs beside the theme file.

theme.build Build receipt {name, tokenCount, componentCount, sizeKB, outputs, warnings, notices}: the theme name; how many tokens (portable plus theme-local) and component targets it overrides; the CSS size in KB; the written outputs {css, cssDts for strict side-effect imports, js, dts, and variantsDts when custom prop values were augmented}; warnings, the defects the author should fix, including exact canonical replacements for deprecated component target keys and declarations the generator dropped; and notices, advisories about a correct theme, such as a font it names but does not load. Resolves to null instead when the theme produced no CSS (nothing to build).

theme.build.check The {check: true} receipt: theme name, an upToDate flag, the stale outputs (each {path, reason: "missing" | "outdated"}), and the full list of checked paths. Writes nothing. Resolves to null, like a normal build, when the theme produces no CSS.

ERR_THEME_LOAD the file cannot be loaded or parsed into a defineTheme() result

ERR_THEME_INVALID the resolved theme is invalid, for example it has no name, a custom Heading type has no standalone rule with a declaration the compiler can emit, or its icon registry cannot be preserved through an import (also rejected in check mode)

ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL the theme name contains a path separator or traversal marker, or a written output resolves outside cwd (including through a symlink): an out path, relative or absolute, or the default outputs beside a theme file outside cwd. Check mode writes nothing, so it refuses only a relative out path that escapes cwd
ERR_CORE_NOT_FOUND @astryxdesign/core/theme cannot be imported; a built, resolvable @astryxdesign/core is required

ERR_CORE_INCOMPATIBLE the installed @astryxdesign/core does not export generateAdaptationCSS and the theme either declares ordered adaptations or has lineage whose adaptation use could not be observed (upgrade core)
ERR_WRITE_FAILED creating the output directory or writing the outputs fails (staged temp files are rolled back)

base.name: themePaletteGenerate
base.description: Generate an author-reviewable palette candidate from JSON input.
prose: themePaletteGenerate()
Generate an author-reviewable palette candidate from JSON input.

Runs the versioned astryx-oklch-v1 recipe against an explicit generation request. It always emits standalone `black` and `white` values that generated TypeScript can import directly into semantic theme tokens; those names are reserved from tonal family IDs. It also defaults family ramps to 21 stops from 0 through 100, repeating exact black and white as endpoints, but accepts any non-empty ordered numeric stop list. Authors may omit those repeated endpoints while retaining the standalone values. The result is a candidate, not an adopted theme palette or an accessibility claim. With an output path it writes the candidate and a detached reproducibility receipt, and leaves existing author-owned files untouched unless overwrite is true. Shared stop numbers keep the same value across layouts, and decimal stops become explicit keys in generated output.
themePaletteGenerate(configPath: string, options?: {out?: string, preview?: string, overwrite?: boolean}, ctx?: {cwd?: string}): ThemePaletteGenerateResponse

options.out string  Where to write the candidate: a path ending in .ts (a TypeScript module) or .json. A sibling <name>.receipt.json is written next to it.

base.name: upgrade
base.description: After bumping @astryxdesign/core, migrate project source with codemods and update copied compositions.
prose: upgrade()
After bumping @astryxdesign/core, migrate project source with codemods and update copied compositions.

Runs the codemods between `from` and the installed Core version, then refreshes the managed agent-docs block. Dry-run by default; `apply` writes changes only after the selected codemods and hooks succeed. Config codemods run before astryx.config is loaded, so they can repair an invalid config. Also updates copied compositions from their install receipts: unchanged files are updated, non-overlapping edits are merged, and conflicts are left untouched. `list` only lists codemods; `registry` only updates copied compositions. Core codemods ship inside the CLI, so a CLI older than the installed Core has none for the releases after its own version: the result then carries `cliBehindCore` with the command that runs the same upgrade on the matching CLI. In global mode: in a project, the CLI runs `upgrade` with the project's own CLI, whichever astryx command started it (in a project with no CLI of its own, the one you started); this function runs the codemods of the package it is imported from. With `cwd` outside a project, `list` lists this release's codemods, `registry` finds no copied compositions, and a migration writes nothing and fails with `ERR_VERSION_DETECT`. See `astryx docs global` and `astryx docs global/who-answers`.
upgrade(options?: UpgradeOptions, ctx?: {cwd?: string}): Promise<UpgradeListResponse | UpgradeRegistryResponse | UpgradeStatusResponse | UpgradeRunResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
options.from string  Version before the dependency bump; the target is the installed @astryxdesign/core (or legacy @xds/core). Required unless list or registry is set.
options.apply boolean false Write changes to disk; otherwise a dry-run preview.
options.force boolean false Run codemods even when from is at/after the installed version.
options.codemod string  Run only this codemod. Optional codemods run only when named here. Setting it also skips copied-composition reconciliation.
options.skipCodemod string[]  Codemod names to exclude (e.g. to re-run past a failure).
options.integration string[]  Explicit integration specifiers to process. Resolved beneath node_modules; absolute paths and . or .. segments are rejected.
options.path string ./src at the project root Source directory to scan. A path you name, in any spelling, is relative to ctx.cwd. When it is omitted, the upgrade scans ./src at the project root.
options.installDeps boolean false Install jscodeshift when it is missing; otherwise a missing jscodeshift throws ERR_DEP_MISSING.

options.registry boolean false Only reconcile copied compositions from their install receipts; from is not required. Cannot be combined with list, from, force, codemod, skipCodemod, integration or installDeps.
options.list boolean false Return the available codemods instead of running any.

ctx.cwd string process.cwd() Any folder in the project to upgrade. The upgrade runs at the project root: the nearest folder at or above it whose package.json declares an Astryx package, or that a workspace whose root declares one lists, found without passing a repository root or counting the home folder. With no such folder, it runs in ctx.cwd. File paths in the result are relative to ctx.cwd, except that a run at the project root names copied-composition paths relative to the scanned source directory.
upgrade.list Every available codemod, oldest→newest, as {name, title, version, optional}, returned when list is set; nothing is run.
upgrade.registry A dry-run or apply receipt for copied compositions, including safe updates, clean merges, conflicts, missing files, and invalid receipts.

upgrade.status A short-circuit outcome (no codemods executed): up_to_date (from is at/after the installed target and no force), no_codemods (none apply to the range), or config_fixable (dry-run preview that a pending config codemod would repair an invalid astryx.config). up_to_date and no_codemods carry the agent-docs summary and, when receipts are found, the copied-composition summary; config_fixable carries configError, configCodemods, suggestedCommand, message, note, and the agent-docs summary. When the installed Core is newer than the CLI, no_codemods and config_fixable also carry cliBehindCore ({cliVersion, command}): this CLI has no codemods for the releases after cliVersion, and command runs the same upgrade with the CLI release that matches the installed Core.

upgrade.run The terminal run receipt: from, to, codemods (count), integrations, agentDocs, agentDocsRefreshed, registryCompositions (when receipts are found), sourcePathFound (false when the resolved path does not exist, so nothing was scanned), filesChanged, transformsApplied, modifiedFiles, protectedFiles, declinedCandidates (left unchanged for manual review, including code a codemod identified but cannot migrate; never incomplete), regenerate (generated files to rebuild, with their commands), errors, and complete. When a protected file still requires a change, including a protected file in regenerate, complete is false and errorCode is ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED; the CLI exits nonzero while preserving the structured receipt. A run that fails after its codemods ran throws instead (see throws), and the thrown AstryxError carries the same receipt on receipt, with complete false and errorCode set to its code. A file in regenerate that nothing protects is such a failure: it is also in errors, and the run throws ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED. When the installed Core is newer than the CLI, it also carries cliBehindCore ({cliVersion, command}): codemods for the releases after cliVersion did not run, and command runs the same upgrade with the matching CLI.

ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT from is missing (and neither list nor registry is set); list and registry are both set; list is combined with from, force, apply, path (non-default), codemod, skipCodemod, integration or installDeps; registry is combined with from, force, codemod, skipCodemod, integration or installDeps; an integration specifier is invalid or not installed; or astryx.config fails to load or validate and no pending config codemod repairs it (when core codemods already wrote files, the error carries their receipt on receipt)
ERR_INVALID_VERSION from is not a valid semver string
ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL path resolves outside the project root

ERR_VERSION_DETECT the project has installed neither @astryxdesign/core nor legacy @xds/core in its own node_modules, nor, for a member its workspace lists, in a folder up to the workspace root (with no Astryx project, in ctx.cwd's own node_modules); with registry, only when copied-composition receipts exist and @astryxdesign/core is not installed
ERR_DEP_MISSING jscodeshift is missing and installDeps is not set, or installing it failed
ERR_UNKNOWN_CODEMOD the version range has codemods but none remain selected: codemod names no codemod in the range, or skipCodemod excludes all of them

ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED one or more codemods failed (including a generated file to regenerate that nothing protects), or a post-codemod hook failed, and no protected file still needs a change (otherwise an upgrade.run receipt with complete: false is returned). The error carries the run's receipt on receipt: the files already changed, each failure in errors, complete: false

ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTION_SOURCE a working-tree protection declaration cannot be read or parsed before writes begin, or after post-codemod hooks rewrite it (the error then carries the receipt on receipt)
List available codemods const r = await upgrade({list: true});
Preview (dry-run) await upgrade({from: '0.0.5'});
Update copied compositions await upgrade({registry: true, apply: true});
Apply changes await upgrade({from: '0.0.5', apply: true});
`astryx upgrade` runs it. Read it with `astryx docs cli/commands/upgrade`.
base._title: Astryx CLI › API › Functions › upgrade()

base.name: validateIntegration
base.description: Validate a single Astryx integration package and report its issues.
prose: validateIntegration()
Validate a single Astryx integration package and report its issues.

Validates exactly ONE integration at a time: the local package rooted at cwd (no `pkg`), or an installed package resolved from cwd/node_modules (`pkg` given). It loads and schema-checks the manifest, verifies each declared contribution root exists, and runs the codemod/template/component/docs/theme validators, returning every finding as an AstryxIntegrationIssue. A missing local manifest is guidance (name null, no issues), not an error, so callers can stay exit-0 in a non-integration directory. It also checks every doc the package ships under its roots (component, template, docs topic, theme, and translation, served or not) against the published authoring type for its kind, as `tsc` would, with the project's own `typescript` (or, where `typescript` is missing or has no JavaScript compiler API, as TypeScript 7 does, the `@typescript/typescript6` it installs): an unknown field, a missing required field, or a value outside a field's type is a warning in `docTypes` naming the field and a fix. A test fixture under `__tests__` in the components or docs root is counted, not checked. Without TypeScript, `docTypes` is `skipped` with a reason.
validateIntegration(pkg?: string, options?: ValidateIntegrationOptions): Promise<ValidateIntegrationResponse>
Import it from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`.
pkg string Installed package name to validate; omit to validate the package rooted at cwd.
options.cwd string Directory to resolve the local package / node_modules from.

integration.validate The result envelope: data.validated, false when nothing was validated — with no package.json at all, data.issues carries one no_package error-severity issue so the command exits 1; with a package.json but no integration manifest, data.issues is empty, which means "not looked at", not "healthy"; data.name and data.version of the validated package (both null when data.validated is false; data.name is (local package) when the local package.json has no readable name), plus data.issues, an AstryxIntegrationIssue[] of {code, severity: warning | error, message, fix?, file?, line?}: fix is the change that resolves the issue, and file and line where it is, relative to the package, when the check knows them; and data.notes when there are any: {code, message, next?} information beside the issues; a note fails nothing by default, and one with next: true counts as a warning under integration check --next, fails integration check --strict --next, and fails --strict from the next minor release. Notes include invalid_cli_command for a cliCommand that was ignored as malformed and cli_peer_version when the running CLI is outside the @astryxdesign/cli peer range of the package, and the package layout findings added after the last minor release, each with its fix in the message: duplicate_component_doc, symlinked_root, unreadable_file, invalid_package_json (no name or version), no_provider_id, and source_without_component_doc for a doc whose file name differs from its source only in letter case where the two still pair; and doc_name_mismatch and unknown_block_component (see docNames and blockComponents); they become warnings in the next minor release. For the commands a topic writes, runner_command (written with a package runner), plain_command (written bare), package_manager_command (written for one package manager) and doc_token (a token that does not parse) notes each give the file, line and the token to write. A doc_target_not_found note names a doc whose replaces or extends names no topic and no guide of the CLI's docs or the package's own (such as a namespace, with the guides below it), so it changes nothing unless an app also installs a package that provides it, and a doc_section_unplaced note a section whose before or after names no section of the topic or guide it extends, so it is added at the end, and a duplicate_guide_replacement note two docs of the package that replace one guide, of which only the last is read; they become warnings in the next minor release. When the manifest loads, data.docTypes holds the doc type check: status (checked | skipped), reason when skipped, typescript, docs (doc values checked), findings ({doc, line, export, type, field, problem: unknown_field | missing_field | wrong_type, severity: warning, message, fix}), unchecked ({doc, reason}: a doc that could not be fully checked, or a root its reader cannot read), and fixtures when the components or docs root holds test fixture docs under __tests__: how many, none of them checked. When the manifest loads, data.docNames lists the component doc names it could not judge: status (checked), findings (always empty; a doc name the module its import names provably does not export is a doc_name_mismatch note, with its fix in the message) and unchecked ({file, name, reason}: a doc whose name differs from the name it is listed under and whose source exports cannot all be read, such as a re-export from another package). When the manifest loads, data.blockComponents lists the component names templates give in exampleFor or componentsUsed that could not be judged: status (checked), findings (always empty; a name neither the package nor Core has, and the template does not import, is an unknown_block_component note, with its fix in the message) and unchecked ({file, name, reason}: a name the template may reach through anything other than named imports and re-exports from Core, React, StyleX, local helpers or the entry of the package itself, such as an import from another package, a default or namespace import, an alias of or member read off an imported binding, require() or a dynamic import(), or a local module that cannot be read, or any name Core would have to resolve when Core is not installed). Since 0.7.3 each import apps cannot use is a note in data.notes, its fix inside the message, listed only: it does not fail this command or integration check --strict, and fails --strict from the next minor release. The codes are component_import_not_exported, component_import_other_package, component_import_missing_name, example_import_not_exported, example_import_missing_name, template_import_not_exported, template_import_outside_root, template_private_import, template_import_missing_name and template_no_default_export. Since 0.7.4 the examples a package ships are checked the same way: component_without_example (a published component no block template shows with exampleFor and isShowcase: true, or names in alsoShowcaseFor), template_category (a template category written as a path, such as components/X), showcase_not_standalone (a showcase that imports server-only code or reads process.env past NODE_ENV) and template_asset_not_packed (a new URL(…, import.meta.url) asset that is missing, or that npm pack --dry-run leaves out of the package). When npm cannot list the package's files, an asset no files entry can reach is still a note, and any other is listed in data.exampleAssets ({status: 'checked', findings: [], unchecked}, present only when it lists any) as {file, asset, reason}; integration check counts them as not compared. When the manifest loads, data.publicImports is {status: 'checked', findings: [], unchecked}: unchecked lists each import the check could not judge, as {file, specifier, reason}, the reason starting example <label>: for an import in a component example: an exports target not built yet; a module whose export list cannot be read in full (CommonJS, or a declaration file it cannot read); a root import in a package with no exports (the root module main names is not read); every name an import (other than a component doc's own component) names that its module does not export, while a TypeScript file in the package has a declare module block for a relative path or the package's own name or a subpath of it, which can add names to that module (a declare module in a comment, declare global, a wildcard such as '*.css', and another package's name do not count; a file whose text has declare module but that cannot be parsed counts); the same for every such name when the package has more than 5,000 files to search for that block; a deep path into build output not built yet in a package with no exports; a template import of Core when @astryxdesign/core is not installed beside the package (a packages/core of the workspace under another name does not count); every import of the package's own name when package.json has no name or a name that is not a bare package name; one entry for the whole check when package.json cannot be read; and an import of a subpath whose exports entry has only a types target, unless it is import type, every binding is an inline type, or every name it imports is a type its types file declares: a value import of a name that file does not declare as a type, a namespace or side-effect import, or any import when the types file cannot be read (it may be build output). integration check counts the unchecked as not compared; they never fail it. data.olderCliNotes ({file, kind: template | namespace, field, message}), for the local package, lists each descriptor field a release before 0.7.4 refuses while the package's CLI peer range admits one, such as stability on a template or namespace doc; it is present only when it has entries, is never counted, and never fails a check.
Validate the local package const r = await validateIntegration();
Validate an installed package await validateIntegration('@acme/astryx-integration');
`astryx doctor integration validate` runs it. Read it with `astryx docs cli/commands/doctor-integration-validate`.

base.name: schemas
base.description: Data shapes, field by field.
prose: Schemas
base._title: Astryx CLI › API › Schemas

base.name: output
base.description: The single JSON envelope every command emits under --json. Success is { apiVersion, type, package?, data, meta? }; failure is { apiVersion, error, code, suggestions? }. Discriminate by checking whether `error` is present.
prose: Output Envelope

The single JSON envelope every command emits under --json. Success is { apiVersion, type, package?, data, meta? }; failure is { apiVersion, error, code, suggestions? }. Discriminate by checking whether `error` is present.
Applies to: astryx --json

Success envelope { apiVersion: number; type: string; package?: string; data: unknown; meta?: { answeredBy?: { cli: string; core: string | null; copy: "project" | "starting" | "matched" | "carried" | "fallback" } } & Record<string, unknown> } no Emitted for every successful command in --json mode: a type discriminator, the package that owns what the response is about, its data payload, and an optional meta object beside data.
apiVersion number yes Version of the JSON envelope contract. Bump on breaking shape changes so consumers can negotiate. Currently 1. Example: 1.
type string yes Names the payload shape. Every value is listed in the response-types enum.

package string no The npm package that owns the one thing the response is about: @astryxdesign/core for a Core component, hook, or template, @astryxdesign/cli for a doc the CLI ships, or the integration package that contributed it. Absent when the response lists things from more than one package; each listed item then names its own package. Example: '@astryxdesign/core'.
data unknown yes The command's payload; its shape depends on type.

meta Record<string, unknown> no Optional, emitted as a sibling of data (never merged in). answeredBy is on every successful result of a release that has it: {cli, core, copy}, the answering CLI version, the Core it pairs with (or null), and which copy answered: project (the project's own CLI), starting (the copy that started the run, in a project with no CLI of its own), matched (the release equal to the project's Core, when the project's own CLI cannot start), carried (outside a project), or fallback (the matched release could not be obtained, so the starting copy answered). A deprecations field is an array of {id, replacements} entries; each stable lifecycle id names the replacement commands without changing the command data. Other fields may be added (spec:AST-017 FR13).

Error envelope { apiVersion: number; error: string; code: ErrorCode; suggestions?: Suggestion[] } no Emitted for every failure in --json mode, including uncaught throws and command-line parse errors, which are converted to this shape.
apiVersion number yes The same contract version carried on the success envelope. Example: 1.
error string yes Human-readable message. It is for people and changes freely, so never branch on it.
code ErrorCode yes Stable, machine-readable identifier; always present, append-only, and never changes meaning. Branch on this. Example: 'ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT'.
suggestions Suggestion[] no Optional "did you mean..." hints, present only when candidates exist.
suggestions[].name string yes The suggested value (e.g. a candidate component name).
suggestions[].reason string no Optional per-item explanation; some call sites emit a bare name with no reason.
The human-readable (text) output is a deterministic projection of this same JSON: --json exposes the structured source of truth, and the default format is rendered from the same data.
`code` is the stable contract; see the error-codes enum (ErrorCode) for the full append-only list. Branch on `code`, never on the `error` prose, which can be reworded or localized at any time.

The process exit code is part of the contract too. Exit 0 means success, and every error envelope exits 1. Some commands also exit 1 with a success envelope when what they report failed: a failed check (doctor and its integration subcommands, integration verify, theme build --check), a gap report that was not delivered, an upgrade left incomplete, or init agent docs refused for a path outside the project. Read the envelope, not the exit code, to tell them apart.

base.name: build
base.description: Build a page: the template to start from, or the workflow playbook (no query)
prose: astryx build
Build a page: the template to start from, or the workflow playbook (no query)

The build-a-page entry point. With no query it returns the how-to-build-a-page playbook; with a query it names the page template to start from (always one: the closest page template, or the app shell when none matches), the next two templates, and the drop-in blocks and idea-specific components and hooks around it.
astryx build [query]
query What you're building (e.g. "analytics dashboard"). Omit for the how-to-build playbook.
--type <domain> Filter the kit to one domain (component|hook|doc|template|theme); doc and theme give an empty kit. One of: component, hook, doc, template, theme.
--limit <n> Max candidates to draw from (default 60)
--verbose Verbose output (every block and component, full descriptions, import paths and match reason)

# Get the playbook
astryx build
# Find the template to start from
astryx build "analytics dashboard" --json

base.name: docs
base.description: Print reference docs
prose: astryx docs
Print reference docs

Reads the reference docs one level at a time: with no topic it lists every topic; a topic lists its sections, each with the key to read it by (a topic with one section prints whole); a topic plus a section prints that section; `--full` prints the whole topic, as does `--dense`. With `--json`, a topic returns its whole doc, as docs() does, and `--index` its section index. A route opens a node of the docs tree: `cli` lists its guides and reference, `cli/api/functions` lists every API function, and `cli/api/functions/search` prints one. A namespace plus a section prints that section from the one guide below it that has it (`astryx docs layout side-panels`). `--depth` reads as far down the tree as you ask, from the doc alone (0) to everything below it (all), and with it `--detail` sets how much of each doc below shows: one line (brief, the default), its sections (compact), or all of it (full).
astryx docs [topic] [section]

topic Doc topic to load (e.g. 'principles'), a docs-tree route (e.g. 'cli/api/functions/search'), or the name of one node of the docs tree: its own name (e.g. 'tokens-color'), or its route without the prefix its name repeats (e.g. 'tokens/color'), where exactly one node answers to it. Omit to list all topics.
section Section to return: its key (from the topic's index), its title, or a unique part of its title (case-insensitive).
--index List the topic's sections and their keys, even for a topic with one section
--full Print the whole topic instead of its sections (text; --json returns the whole topic unless --index). Cannot be set with --index

--depth <levels> How many levels of the docs tree to read below a namespace: 0 for the namespace alone, 1 for its children (what a read without --depth shows), all for everything below it. On the topic list, where a namespace otherwise lists alone, it names the docs below each one by the route that opens them, one line each. With it on a namespace read, --detail sets how much of each doc below shows: brief (one line each, the default), compact (with its sections), or full; the topic list is one line per doc whatever the detail

# List topics
astryx docs
# A topic's sections
astryx docs theme
# A whole topic as JSON
astryx docs spacing --json
# One section
astryx docs theme quick-start
# The CLI docs tree
astryx docs cli
# Every CLI doc, one line each
astryx docs cli --depth all
# Every route in the docs tree, one line each
astryx docs --depth all
# The integration guides as one read
astryx docs authoring --depth all --detail full
# One API function
astryx docs cli/api/functions/search
# A whole guide
astryx docs authoring/quick-start --full
0 success
1 unknown topic or route, a section that matches no section or more than one, or a --depth that is not a number of levels or all

It never fails a check because the folder has no project.

Check integration component names, replacements, and documented props

Compares one local or installed integration with Core component names. A conflict is allowed and exits successfully, but the report recommends renaming and gives the exact --package command for an intentional overlap. It also checks each component's replaces: in a package that declares the CLI range that turns replacement on, a missing Core target, an invalid value, a component named after a different Core component, or two replacements for one Core component is an error. Without TypeScript it prints one line saying the comparison was skipped. It also warns on each `{@link}` in a component doc's text that names no doc.

base.name: gap-report
base.description: Report a missing component or feature to the package that owns it
prose: astryx gap-report
Report a missing component or feature to the package that owns it

Reports a missing component, variant, layout, styling, accessibility, API, or documentation capability to the package that owns it: the --package you name, else the integration whose component replaces it, else the one package that provides the component, else Core. Every configured handler receives the report: the project config handler first, then each integration handler in config order. Public handlers run only with --confirm-public; internal handlers always run. A failing handler does not stop the others. With no handler it files a GitHub issue for the owning package, only with --confirm-public (without it nothing is sent), or returns the package's issues URL when that is not on GitHub. With --to <package>, the report goes only to that integration's issues URL instead, under the same --confirm-public rule. When loaded integrations name their own issues URLs, the output lists every destination: an agent asks the person where to file and passes their choice with --to; it never picks a package itself, and without a choice the default is used. The report records whether an agent or a person ran it.
astryx gap-report [component]
component Component or design-system area the gap is about, up to 120 characters. Required unless --list-categories is set.
--category <category> Gap category (run --list-categories for values). Required unless --list-categories is set.
--reason <reason> What capability was missing or difficult, up to 2000 characters. Required unless --list-categories is set.
--additional-context <text> Optional additional context, up to 8000 characters

--package <pkg> Package that owns the gap: @astryxdesign/core or a loaded integration. Overrides automatic routing, which picks the integration whose component replaces the named Core component, else the one package that provides it, else Core; needed when more than one package provides the component
--confirm-public Allow public delivery: public handlers run, and a GitHub issues URL gets an issue filed with your gh login
--to <package> Send the report only to this loaded integration's issues URL, as the person chose; the destinations the output lists are the choices
--list-categories List valid report categories, and the destinations when there is more than one, without filing; the component and the other gap-report options are refused with ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT

# List categories
astryx gap-report --list-categories
# Prepare a report (nothing public happens without --confirm-public)
astryx gap-report Button --category missing_variant --reason 'Need a compact size'
# File where the person chose
astryx gap-report Button --category missing_variant --reason 'Need a compact size' --to @acme/widgets
0 filed, routed-only, confirmation required, skipped, or categories listed
1 failed or partial delivery, invalid input, or ambiguous routing

base.name: init
base.description: Initialize the design system in your project
prose: astryx init
Initialize the design system in your project

Non-interactive project setup (no prompts, so it behaves the same for humans, agents, and CI). By default it writes the agent-docs block, including guidance from configured integrations, to AGENTS.md and to the Claude Code file the project has (CLAUDE.md, else .claude/CLAUDE.md; when CLAUDE.md exists, a block in .claude/CLAUDE.md is removed, unless the project ignores CLAUDE.md, in which case a .claude/CLAUDE.md the project commits keeps a copy), and a one-line import of AGENTS.md to GEMINI.md unless GEMINI.md already imports it. It then prints getting-started steps. Agent docs go to the project root: the nearest folder at or above this one whose package.json declares an @astryxdesign package, else the nearest with any package.json, else this folder. The search stops at a repository root and never counts the home folder. In the home folder, or in a settings folder in it such as ~/.gemini outside a project, no agent docs are written. Every folder of the home folder whose name starts with a dot is a settings folder, and such a folder itself never counts as a project, even with a package.json; a project inside one, such as an agent worktree with its own package.json, works. The managed block is written whatever ignore rules or generated markers say; the text around it is never changed. --features and --all print only the chosen features' guidance (no getting-started steps); the theme feature also writes an annotated theme template. Outside a project it writes the same files but prints no step that sets up a project: no getting-started steps, and no step that adds a theme to an app. --user writes the computer-level agent text instead (see the flag), in any folder, and touches nothing in the folder. The CLI installed for the computer also keeps that text current in the background, unless --user --remove-agents turned it off; package install scripts, project setup, and upgrade never write it.
astryx init

--features <list> Comma-separated features: agents (agent docs), theme (writes theme.template.ts), template (prints the page-building commands; writes no file). An unknown feature exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_FEATURE. Refused with --all or --remove-agents
--all Install all features (agents, theme, template); refused with --features. Prints their guidance instead of the getting-started steps

--remove-agents Remove the managed block from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules, .hermes.md and HERMES.md, at the project root (where init writes them) and in this folder (deleting AGENTS.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md when only init's heading is left, and GEMINI.md when nothing is left) and do nothing else. Below the project root, a project-root agent file whose block resolves outside the project is left as it is, with a note. --features, --all, --agent and --agent-docs-path are refused; a file written with --agent-docs-path keeps its block

--user Write or refresh the computer-level agent text instead of setting up the folder: one skill file, ~/.agents/skills/astryx/SKILL.md, which most coding agents read, linked into the skill folders of agents that read only their own (~/.claude/skills always; Kiro, Windsurf, Letta, Xcode's coding assistant, and ~/.config/agents/skills when that folder exists): a folder symlink with a relative target, a junction on Windows, or a copy where neither can be made. Continue, whose scanner skips links, gets a managed copy, refreshed with the file. It tells agents anywhere on the computer that Astryx is there, when it is relevant, and to start with astryx search. Records the links it made in astryx/settings.json in the per-user configuration folder, so removal removes exactly those; the CLI installed for the computer refreshes the file in the background after each upgrade. Works in any folder. A file without the Astryx markers, one edited since Astryx wrote it, or a symlink, is kept as it is, and so is anything at a link target that Astryx did not create. Warns, and still writes, when no astryx command on the computer runs the Astryx CLI. With --remove-agents it removes the file, the links, and the copy instead and records that the text is turned off. --features, --all, --agent and --agent-docs-path are refused

A path in the home folder itself, or in a settings folder in it outside a project (such as ~/.claude or ~/.claude/hooks), is refused with a note (exit 0), and nothing is written. Used only when agent docs are installed

name Contribution name: PascalCase for component (AcmeWidget); lowercase kebab-case for template, codemod, and theme (account-card); letters, digits, _ and - for doc; the literal guidance line for agent-doc

base.name: integration check
base.description: The CI check for an integration package's own build: every source check, run in continuous integration or a typecheck script, against the package in the current folder
prose: astryx integration check
The CI check for an integration package's own build: every source check, run in continuous integration or a typecheck script, against the package in the current folder

Takes no package argument: it runs the four `doctor integration` checks, `validate`, `components`, `templates`, and `docs`, against the integration package in the current folder, which is where its own build runs it. It prints each result as that check prints it, then a summary with the errors, warnings, and skipped work of each, and exits 1 when any of the four would exit 1 on its own. With `--strict` it also exits 1 on any warning and on any check, or comparison within a check, that did not run, such as a package with no `astryx.integration.*` or a comparison skipped because the project has no TypeScript, or prop types not judged because its TypeScript is older than 4.8: it adds no check, and lists each of those again as an error, after the checks, in their own issue format. That is the line for the package's own build, so its docs, types, and links stay in sync: run it as a `ci` step, or add `"typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && astryx integration check --strict"` to the scripts in package.json. Its exit codes and JSON are a contract for the builds that run it: a new check, or a new failure code, joins only in a minor release that names it in the release notes. A patch can still ship a Core component, template, or CLI topic whose name conflicts with one of yours. Run `integration check` on every build; run `integration verify` before you publish, to check that the packed package works in an app. To check an installed integration by name, run the `doctor integration` subcommands with its package name. Outside a package, it writes nothing, `validate` reports one `no_package` issue, and it exits 1.
astryx integration check

--strict Also exit 1 on any warning and on any check that did not run. A new check or failure code joins only in a minor release, named in the release notes; until then, a malformed cliCommand is reported as a note (invalid_cli_command) that fails nothing.

--next Also count the findings the next minor release turns into warnings (the notes marked next) as warnings now, so --strict --next fails on them. Run it to fix them ahead of the release; every run says how many there are.

# In CI, as the typecheck script: add "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && astryx integration check --strict" to package.json
integration check --strict
# Errors only, while you fix the warnings a package already has
integration check
# Fix ahead: fail on the findings the next minor release will fail on
integration check --strict --next
# Read the result as JSON
integration check --strict --json
# Before you publish: check that the packed package works in an app
integration verify
0 no check fails on its own; with --strict, also no warning, and every check ran
1 a check fails on its own (an error); with --strict, also any warning, or a check that did not run
Outside a project (`own`): it does what the description above says it does outside a project.

base.name: swizzle
base.description: Copy component source for customization
prose: astryx swizzle
Copy component source for customization

Ejects a component's source from the resolved @astryxdesign/core (or its owning integration) into your project for deep customization. Every import in the copy names a file the copy holds or a path the package exports: names the package exports come from the package, and every internal module the component needs is copied beside it in the package's folder layout. Tests, stories and docs are not copied. It lists the npm packages the copy imports, with the ranges the owner package declares, to install if your project lacks them. An output folder swizzle owns (one the copy creates, an empty one, or one it marked before) gets an astryx-swizzle.json marker naming each package its copies came from, so @astryxdesign/build's Babel, PostCSS and Vite integrations, and withAstryx() under webpack, compile the copy below your theme. With no name it lists the swizzlable components. An integration component that replaces a Core component is what that Core name copies; --package @astryxdesign/core copies the original. --list lists Core components, including one an integration replaces.
astryx swizzle [component]
component Component name to copy (e.g. 'Button'). Omit to list the swizzlable components.
--output <dir> Output directory. Default: ./components/astryx.
--package <pkg> Scope to a specific owning package. Use @astryxdesign/core to copy an original replaced by an integration component
--list List the swizzlable Core components, including any that an integration component replaces

-f, --overwrite Replace the component's existing files. Without it, existing files fail the command with ERR_FILE_EXISTS and nothing is written. A helper an earlier swizzle wrote is reused when it is the same and is never replaced by a copy that carries it: a different one stays, and this copy writes its own under a version-suffixed name. Swizzling the component whose folder holds that helper counts it as one of that component's own files. A changed private attribute owner module, or a style module it imports, fails the command without --overwrite and is replaced with it

# List swizzlable components
astryx swizzle --list
# Eject a component
astryx swizzle Button
# Copy a replaced Core original
astryx swizzle SideNav --package @astryxdesign/core
0 success
1 unknown or ambiguous component, no source on disk, a path escape, or existing files without --overwrite

base.description: List, show, or scaffold page and block templates
prose: astryx template
List, show, or scaffold page and block templates

One entry point for the template family: with no name it lists the discovered templates; with a name it shows the source or a layout skeleton, or scaffolds it into the project at a target path. astryx template [name] [path]
name Template id (see --list). Omit it to list the templates.

path Where to scaffold the template, relative to the project root. A path that ends in .tsx, .ts, .jsx, .js, .mjs, .cjs, .css, .scss, .json, .md or .html is the file to write; any other path is a directory, which receives page.tsx for a page template or the block's own file name for a block. Omit it to print the source.
--list List available templates (narrow with --type and --package) and do nothing else: <name>, <path>, --skeleton and --overwrite are refused
--type <type> Filter by template type: page or block. One of: page, block.
--package <pkg> Narrow to templates from a specific package. Use @astryxdesign/core to select an original hidden by an integration replacement.

--skeleton Show layout skeleton with spatial annotations (padding, gap, nesting) instead of the source. Needs <name>. It writes nothing, so <path> and --overwrite are refused with ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT

--cdn [path] Write the no-build-step CDN starter page and do nothing else: <name>, --list, --skeleton, --type and --package are refused. The page goes to the --cdn value, else to <path>, else cdn.template.html, and that path is always the file itself. A value right after --cdn (anything not starting with -) is taken as that path
-f, --overwrite Replace an existing target file. Without it an existing file is refused (ERR_FILE_EXISTS) and an existing CDN page is left as is

base.name: theme build
base.description: Compile standalone themes or one keyed theme family
prose: astryx theme build
Compile standalone themes or one keyed theme family

Compiles defineTheme() sources through the same theme pipeline into scoped CSS, standard ESM, and type declarations. Ordinary mode writes one complete set per theme. --family combines one selected extension tree into the three files named by the required --family-key, ready for one CSS load and identity-only switching. With --check it writes nothing and reports source drift. --icons-specifier keeps its existing generated-module behavior. It prints one line per built theme and one line naming fonts the themes do not load; --detail full adds the install example and the font recipe, once for a batch.
astryx theme build <files...>
files Path to a theme file that calls defineTheme(), resolved against cwd.

--family Build the selected extension family into one keyed CSS, JS, and declaration set, written beside the family root theme file, which must be inside the working directory to build (ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL); --check only reads, so it compares outputs anywhere. Requires --family-key; refused with --out or --watch (ERR_THEME_INVALID)
--family-key <key> Lower-kebab filename stem required with --family and refused without it; must differ from every member name (ERR_THEME_INVALID)

-o, --out <path> Output CSS file path, relative or absolute; the .js and .d.ts are written beside it (default: <theme name>.css next to the source). A build writes only inside the working directory, the defaults beside the source too (ERR_PATH_TRAVERSAL); --check writes nothing, so it compares outputs anywhere and refuses only a relative path that escapes the working directory. Single theme only: refused with more than one file or with --family (ERR_THEME_INVALID)

base.name: theme palette generate
base.description: Generate an OKLCH palette candidate for human review
prose: astryx theme palette generate
Generate an OKLCH palette candidate for human review

Reads an explicit JSON request and runs the versioned astryx-oklch-v1 recipe. The command defaults to 21 stops (0 through 100) but accepts any non-empty ordered numeric stop list, including decimals. Stops apply to every family in the request. Authors may omit the repeated endpoints with a custom list; standalone exact black and white values remain available in every candidate. For anchors, exact preserves the chosen color at its mode and stop; bounded allows movement within maxDeltaE; flexible uses the color as guidance. Without --out it prints a preview. With --out it writes a candidate file and detached receipt. --preview writes a standardized, self-contained HTML review artifact. TypeScript output is directly importable and contains no generator dependency. JSON is also supported. Existing author-owned files are left untouched unless --overwrite is explicit. When used in a theme integration, keep the palette request under the theme slug, write the candidate and receipt under that same slug, import the candidate from the theme source, and keep all three inside the theme directory. The package ships that directory as one source unit for discovery and explicit eject, while apps use its built exports.
astryx theme palette generate <config>
config Path to a JSON file holding a TonalPaletteGenerationInput (the object generateTonalPalette() takes), resolved within cwd.
-o, --out <path> Write a candidate TypeScript or JSON file and a sibling receipt
--preview <path> Write a self-contained HTML preview page; the path must end in .html
-f, --overwrite Replace existing candidate, receipt, and preview files. Without it, if any of them exists, nothing is written

astryx theme palette generate themes/ocean/palette.config.json
# Write candidate and receipt
astryx theme palette generate themes/ocean/palette.config.json --out themes/ocean/tokens/ocean.palette.ts
# Write candidate, receipt, and review preview
astryx theme palette generate themes/ocean/palette.config.json --out themes/ocean/tokens/ocean.palette.ts --preview themes/ocean/tokens/ocean.palette.html

base.name: upgrade
base.description: Update your code after upgrading Astryx, and refresh ShadCN-copied components
prose: astryx upgrade
Update your code after upgrading Astryx, and refresh ShadCN-copied components

Migrates project source from a previous Astryx version to the installed one by running the registered codemods, and refreshes the fully rendered managed agent-docs block when Core or configured integration guidance changes. Dry-run by default. --apply writes codemod and receipt changes, runs hooks, then refreshes agent docs. Anything a post-codemod hook prints goes to stderr, so stdout carries only the result. Run from a folder inside a project, it upgrades that project and names files in the result relative to the folder you ran it in. ShadCN-copied compositions are checked automatically during a normal upgrade, or alone with --registry. Outside a project, --list lists the codemods this release ships and --registry finds no copied compositions to update; a migration writes nothing and fails with ERR_VERSION_DETECT, because no installed Core names its target.
astryx upgrade

--from <version> Previous version before the dependency upgrade; required unless --list or --registry is set. The target is the installed @astryxdesign/core version, or legacy @xds/core when @astryxdesign/core is not installed
--apply Write changes to disk; without it, the run is a dry run
--force Run codemods even if --from is newer than the installed version

--codemod <name> Run only the named codemod. Optional codemods run only when named here; a normal run skips them. Also skips the check of ShadCN-copied compositions. An unknown name exits 1 with ERR_UNKNOWN_CODEMOD when the version range has codemods
--skip-codemod <name...> Exclude named codemods (repeatable). Re-run past a failed codemod by skipping it.
--integration <package> Explicit integration specifier (repeatable). Resolved beneath node_modules; absolute paths and . or .. segments are rejected.

--path <dir> Source directory to scan, relative to where you run the command, however you spell it. Without --path, the project's src folder, from any folder in the project. Default: ./src at the project root.
--install-deps Install jscodeshift when it is missing. Without it, a missing jscodeshift fails the command with ERR_DEP_MISSING

--registry Only update ShadCN-copied compositions from their install receipts: unchanged files are updated, edits that do not overlap are merged, and conflicts are left untouched; --from is not required. Combining it with --list, --from, --force, --codemod, --skip-codemod, --integration or --install-deps exits 1 with ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT
--list List available codemods and do nothing else. Every other flag is refused, as is --registry (exit 1)

# List available codemods
astryx upgrade --list --json
# Update ShadCN-copied compositions
astryx upgrade --registry --apply
# Apply a migration
astryx upgrade --from 0.1.0 --apply
0 success, including complete dry-run previews and runs whose only findings are manual migrations

1 missing or invalid --from, --registry with --list or a migration flag, a --path escape, no installed @astryxdesign/core (or legacy @xds/core), jscodeshift missing and not installed by --install-deps, an astryx.config that fails validation and that no pending config codemod repairs, an unreadable or invalid protection declaration, a protected file that still requires a codemod change, a generated file that must be regenerated, an unknown codemod, a codemod or post-codemod hook failure, or unresolved registry items
Outside a project (`own`): it does what the description above says it does outside a project.
It runs `upgrade()` from `@astryxdesign/cli/api`. Read it with `astryx docs cli/api/functions/upgrade`.

In global mode: in a project, upgrade runs the codemods of the project's own CLI, whichever astryx command you start; in a project with no CLI of its own, the astryx command you started runs them, so install the CLI at the new Core's version first (`astryx doctor` prints the command). Outside a project, `--list` lists this version's codemods, `--registry` finds no copied compositions, and a migration writes nothing and stops with `ERR_VERSION_DETECT`. See `astryx docs global` and `astryx docs global/who-answers`.
A CLI older than your Core

Core codemods ship inside the CLI, so a CLI older than the installed @astryxdesign/core has none for the releases after its own version. upgrade then says it cannot finish, never reports your code as up to date, and prints the same upgrade pinned to the CLI release that matches your Core, such as `cd <project> && npx @astryxdesign/cli@<core-version> upgrade --from <old-version> --path <source-dir> --apply`. It changes to the folder this run used and names the directory it scanned as an absolute path, both with symbolic links resolved, so pasted from any folder it upgrades the same code. It is written for a POSIX shell (sh, bash, zsh), or for PowerShell on Windows, with each argument quoted for that shell; cmd.exe is not a target. The codemods this CLI has still run. It exits 0, so a script checks the JSON: the result carries `cliBehindCore` with `cliVersion` (the newest release this CLI has codemods for) and `command`.
Protected files

Codemods never write to a file your project marks as generated, vendored, or ignored. upgrade reads these marks from the files on disk, so the answer is the same with any version control, or none. A file is protected when:
a `.gitattributes` file marks it `linguist-generated` or `linguist-vendored`
its leading comment says `@generated`, `@partially-generated`, or `Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT.`
a `.gitignore`, or the `.hgignore` at the project root, excludes it
it is an installed dependency (such as anything in `node_modules`), is inside `.git`, `.hg`, or `.sl`, is a symbolic link, or is outside the project

upgrade does not scan installed dependencies or version-control folders at all, including through a symbolic link: a symlinked `node_modules`, or a link whose target is inside one or inside a package store such as `.yarn/cache`, is skipped. Other symbolically linked folders are scanned so a change they need is reported, but nothing is written through them.

Rules work as they do in Git: a later rule wins, so `linguist-generated=false` or a `!` line in an ignore file returns a file to normal handling. A folder name such as `dist` or `generated` protects nothing by itself. If a protection file cannot be read or parsed, upgrade stops with ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTION_SOURCE before it writes anything.

# .gitattributes
generated/** linguist-generated=true
vendor/** linguist-vendored=true

# A later rule returns one authored file to normal handling
generated/hand-authored.ts linguist-generated=false

When a codemod would change a protected file, upgrade makes the change only in memory and leaves the file as it is. The rest of the upgrade goes ahead. With --apply, your other files are written, then upgrade runs the `hooks.postCodemod` commands from astryx.config (see `astryx docs authoring config`) and checks the protected files again. If one still needs the change, the run is incomplete: it exits 1, prints ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED with each file and the rule that protects it, and does not refresh the agent docs. Regenerate or edit those files, then run the same upgrade again. A dry run reports the same files and writes nothing.

With --json, the receipt says `complete: false` and `errorCode: "ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED"`. `modifiedFiles` lists the files upgrade changed (or would change), and `protectedFiles` lists each blocked file with its `reasons`, `declarations` (the rules that protect it), `codemods`, and `commands`. A generated file can name the command that rebuilds it on a `Command:` line in its header, such as `// Command: pnpm run gen:panel`; upgrade prints it as `Regenerate with: <command>` and lists it in `commands`.

A protected file a codemod cannot parse, such as a vendored bundle written for another toolchain, cannot need a change the codemod can prove, and upgrade never writes it. upgrade skips it, lists it under `declinedCandidates` with the parse error and where it occurred, and carries on; on its own it does not fail the run. If another codemod in the same upgrade still requires a change to that file (the 0.6.0 theme selector migration, for one, adds a TODO comment above a selector it cannot parse), the file is listed once, under `protectedFiles`, and the run is incomplete as for any protected file. A file upgrade owns that does not parse still fails the run with ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED.
Manual migrations and regeneration

Some changes a codemod can find but not make. upgrade lists them in the result, so a script can keep the rest of the run and act on each. Code a codemod can identify but cannot migrate safely is a manual migration: upgrade lists each file with its line, the codemod and what to change, finishes the run, and exits 0. With --json they are in `declinedCandidates`, one row per file (each finding in `reason` starts with `manual migration needed (<codemod>):`, and a file with several findings lists them all, joined by `; `), and `complete` stays true. A generated file that must be rebuilt is listed in `regenerate` with the command that rebuilds it, such as `astryx theme build`: a protected generated file a codemod still needs to change (also in `protectedFiles`), or a generated output a codemod found out of date (also in `protectedFiles`, with the rule that protects it, when the project marks it generated). With --apply, upgrade runs your `hooks.postCodemod` commands and checks again. If a protected file still needs rebuilding, the run is incomplete exactly as for any protected file: it exits 1 and the result says `complete: false` and `errorCode: "ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED"`. If a file nothing protects still needs rebuilding, no protected file is in the way: the codemod could not make a required change, so it is also in `errors` and the run fails with `ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED`, as described below. Either way, rebuild it, then run the same upgrade again. When a codemod also failed, the failure is reported as below, and the receipt it carries still lists `declinedCandidates` and `regenerate`, unless a protected file to regenerate also remains, in which case the run returns `ERR_CODEMOD_PROTECTED` with the failure in `errors`.
A failed codemod

When a codemod or a `hooks.postCodemod` command fails, upgrade still makes every other change, exits 1 with ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED, and does not refresh the agent docs. With --json, the result is the usual error, `{"error": ..., "code": "ERR_CODEMOD_FAILED"}`, plus a `receipt`: the same fields a finished run returns, with `complete: false`, each failure in `errors`, and every file upgrade changed (or would change) in `modifiedFiles`, so a script can review, keep, or revert them. An error that stops the run after codemods have written files, such as an astryx.config that fails validation, carries a `receipt` too. Rerun past a failed codemod with --skip-codemod.
base._title: Astryx CLI › Commands › astryx upgrade

base.name: several
base.description: `astryx component` accepts exact selectors as a variadic positional argument. With no selector it browses the catalog. With one selector it keeps the normal single-component response. With two or more it prints one complete ordered batch…
prose: Look up several components

`astryx component` accepts exact selectors as a variadic positional argument. With no selector it browses the catalog. With one selector it keeps the normal single-component response. With two or more it prints one complete ordered batch receipt.

Several component docs astryx component Button Badge Text
astryx --json component Button Badge Text
Every selector gets one row in input order. Duplicate selectors stay duplicate rows. A missing or ambiguous component does not hide successful neighbors or stop later selectors from resolving.

A batch accepts at most 100 selectors, including duplicates, in every projection mode. A larger request returns a top-level `ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT` before any component resolves. It emits no `component.batch` receipt and no partial results.
Focused component controls apply to every found row. Use the same control you use for one component:

Focused batch lookups astryx --json component Button Card --props
astryx component Button Card --source
astryx component Button Card --showcase
astryx component Button Card --blocks
astryx component Button Card --detail compact
astryx component Button Card --lang dense
astryx component Button Card --package @astryxdesign/core
base._title: Astryx CLI › Component lookups › Look up several components

base.name: selectors
base.description: A selector is an exact component identity, not free-text search. Use one of these forms:
prose: Selector forms
A selector is an exact component identity, not free-text search. Use one of these forms:
`Button` for an unqualified component name.
`widgets/Button` for a component in an unscoped package.
`@acme/widgets/Button` for a component in a scoped package.
`@acme/widgets@1.2.3/Button` to require that exact installed package version.

A version qualifies the package, never the component. The lookup does not fall through to another installed version. An unqualified name owned by several installed packages is `ambiguous` and lists every candidate. Use a package-qualified selector or `--package` to choose one.
`astryx discover` remains free-text package discovery. Its words form one query; they are not component batch selectors.
base._title: Astryx CLI › Component lookups › Selector forms

base.name: output
base.description: JSON uses `component.batch` with `{count, results}`. Each row echoes `selector` and has one status: `found`, `not_found`, `ambiguous`, or `error`. A found row carries the normal single-component `{type, data}` under `result`. Failed rows…
prose: Batch output and exit status

JSON uses `component.batch` with `{count, results}`. Each row echoes `selector` and has one status: `found`, `not_found`, `ambiguous`, or `error`. A found row carries the normal single-component `{type, data}` under `result`. Failed rows carry `code` and `error`, plus `suggestions` or `candidates` when available.

Outcome and duplicate examples astryx --json component Button Badge                 # all found, exit 0
astryx --json component Button MissingWidget         # mixed, exit 1
astryx --json component MissingWidget MissingPanel   # all failed, exit 1
astryx --json component Button Button                # two ordered rows, exit 0
A complete failed JSON receipt astryx --json component MissingWidget MissingPanel

The same receipt in text mode Component batch

count: 2

Results

MissingWidget

selector: MissingWidget
status:   not_found
code:     ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT
error:    No component named "MissingWidget"

MissingPanel

selector: MissingPanel
status:   not_found
code:     ERR_UNKNOWN_COMPONENT
error:    No component named "MissingPanel"

The CLI emits every row first, then exits 1 when any row is not `found`. This includes mixed receipts and receipts where every row failed. JSON and text use the same exit status. A batch where every row is `found` exits 0.

base.name: api
base.description: The argument shape chooses the response shape. Omit the argument for the catalog, pass a string for the existing single-component response, and pass an array for `component.batch`. An array always means batch, including empty and one-item…
prose: Programmatic API

The argument shape chooses the response shape. Omit the argument for the catalog, pass a string for the existing single-component response, and pass an array for `component.batch`. An array always means batch, including empty and one-item arrays, so filtering a selector list cannot silently change the response type. The published `ComponentBatchResponse` specializes the shared `BatchResponse` and `BatchRow` types.

import {component} from '@astryxdesign/cli/api';

const catalog = await component(); // component.list
const button = await component('Button'); // component.detail
const empty = await component([]); // component.batch, count 0
const oneRow = await component(['Button']); // component.batch, count 1
const batch = await component(['Button', 'Badge']); // component.batch, count 2
await component(Array(101).fill('Button')); // ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT before lookup

base.name: options
prose: Options
argv none The command-line arguments, without the command name.
cwd the process's working folder The folder the run works in. It must exist.
cliCommand the package manager's name The command your users type, such as acme astryx: a non-blank single line of at most 120 characters, with no surrounding spaces.
declinedProjectCli none Why you did not run the project's own CLI, such as untrusted: a non-blank single line of at most 120 characters. That CLI then never runs.

roots none Your package sets, in order of preference: folders whose node_modules each hold a CLI, the Core of the same release, and integrations. A run never installs a release; it takes the release a project needs from the first set that holds it.
integrations none Integrations you approve for use outside a project, by package name.
discoverSources none Your own discover sources. astryx discover reports each as the host's.
base._title: Astryx CLI › Host entry › Options

base.name: result
base.description: It resolves with `{status, packages}`: the exit status the CLI's own command would exit with, and each package the run used, with its version and whether it came from the project or a package set.
prose: Result and errors
It resolves with `{status, packages}`: the exit status the CLI's own command would exit with, and each package the run used, with its version and whether it came from the project or a package set.
When another release answers from one of your package sets through its own host entry, that entry runs in the same process with the same inputs, and the call resolves with its result.
It rejects with a `TypeError`, before anything runs, for an unknown option or an invalid value, and with an `Error` when a run already started in the process. Start each run in a new process.
base._title: Astryx CLI › Host entry › Result and errors

base.name: process-ends
base.description: Like the CLI's own command, a run ends the process with its exit status, and the call never resolves, when it:
prose: When the process ends instead
Like the CLI's own command, a run ends the process with its exit status, and the call never resolves, when it:
prints help or the version (`--help`, `-h`, `help`, `--version`, `-V`, `--version --json`);
rejects the command line, such as an unknown command or option;
reports an error it stops on, including every error in `--json` mode;
meets an unexpected error;
hands the run to another CLI's own command: the project's CLI when you pass no `declinedProjectCli`, or a package set whose CLI has no host entry.
